title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE VALEDICTORY CEREMONY OF THE CENTENARY CELEBRATIONS OF SHRI RAM COLLEGE OF COMMERCE
subtitle: INDIA HAS THE BEST POOL OF YOUNG TALENT IN THE WORLD AS DEMONSTRATED IN COLLEGES LIKE SRCC: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 6:40PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced the Valedictory Ceremony of the Centenary Celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) in New Delhi today (November 18, 2026).
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that the country's leading educational institutions must evolve into world-class institutions. It will not only help in realizing the national vision of transforming India into a Global Knowledge Superpower but also attract talented students from both within India and abroad for higher education.
The President said that during the last ten years, India has remained one of the fastest-growing large economies in the world. The country has achieved unprecedented expansion of infrastructure, revolutionary digital transformation, financial inclusion and social development. There is a conducive start-up ecosystem. ‘Ease of Doing Business’ has been given high priority. At the same time, effective welfare measures have been implemented with the approach of leaving no targeted beneficiary uncovered. Around 50 crore fellow citizens have come out of extreme poverty in recent years. These achievements have been made possible amidst several challenges in the global environment, characterised by uncertainties and ongoing conflicts. The students at this college are fortunate to witness the resilience and success of our economy and learn from it. They will utilise this learning to further accelerate our journey of development.
The President said that Bharat is expanding its economic role on the global stage with a new energy and outlook. Our youth will be driving our ambitious endeavours. India has the largest young population in the world and  it also has the best pool of young talent in the world as demonstrated in colleges like SRCC.
The President said that ‘Of India, by India, and for India’ is the approach with which our youth should define their aspirations and roles. In this context, ‘by India’ implies that the society and institutions have contributed to the development of capabilities of students. Therefore, they have a special responsibility towards the society and the country.
The President was happy to note that the students of SRCC have been scoring high marks and securing top positions in examinations. She said that students of SRCC should demonstrate that wealth creation leads to nation-building; should do well for themselves and also create opportunities for others, especially for the less privileged; should achieve world-class excellence while remaining rooted in the noble Indian values; should use state-of-the-art technologies responsibly with sensitivity; and should pursue professional excellence with empathy, ethics and morality. She expressed confidence that members of the SRCC family will continue to contribute towards the building of Viksit Bharat by 2047 and the glorious journey of our country even beyond.

title: Vice-President Graces Silver Jubilee Celebrations and 8th Annual Convocation of Vardhman Mahavir Medical College and Safdarjung Hospital in New Delhi
subtitle:
Vice-President Calls upon graduating doctors to uphold compassion, integrity and scientific temper; says a medical degree is a commitment to humanity

Viksit Bharat Must Also Be a Swasth Bharat: Vice-President Highlights India’s Healthcare Transformation

Technology Must Never Replace the Human Connection Between Doctor and Patient: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 6:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today graced the Silver Jubilee Celebrations and 8th Annual Convocation of Vardhman Mahavir Medical College (VMMC) and Safdarjung Hospital as the Chief Guest at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. He distributed medals to outstanding postgraduate and undergraduate students on the occasion.
Congratulating the VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital fraternity on completing 25 years of dedicated service to medical education, healthcare and society, the Vice-President said that twenty-five years represented trust earned, lives touched, knowledge created and service rendered. He described the occasion as a celebration of a legacy of learning, healing and nation-building.
Referring to the remarkable expansion of India’s healthcare and medical education sectors, the Vice-President said that under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the dynamism of Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, the country has made tremendous progress.
The Vice-President said that this expansion reflects the growing reach of higher education and India’s commitment to strengthening its healthcare system. The focus is now increasingly on quality healthcare, medical education, research and innovation, he added.
Emphasising that a medical degree is fundamentally a commitment to humanity, he said that the true measure of a doctor lies in the lives improved and dignity preserved. He urged the young doctors to let empathy accompany their expertise, integrity guide their decisions and scientific temper strengthen their professional practice.
Technology, he stressed, must never replace the human connection between a doctor and a patient. He called upon the graduates to listen patiently, communicate honestly and treat every individual with dignity, irrespective of their financial circumstances or social background.
Referring to the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047 articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice-President said that a healthy, educated and empowered population would form the foundation of India’s national progress. The Prime Minister has repeatedly emphasised that a Viksit Bharat must also be a Swasth Bharat, he said, adding that initiatives such as Ayushman Bharat reflect the country’s commitment to making quality healthcare accessible and affordable to all.
Urging the graduating doctors to keep Nation First – Rashtra Pratham – in all their thoughts and actions, he encouraged them to dedicate their knowledge to healing and their compassion to inspiring others. He also urged everyone to say ‘No to Drugs’.
Recalling that VMMC bears the name of Lord Mahavira, the Vice-President observed that the philosophy of ‘Live and Let Live’ resonates deeply with the noble mission of the medical profession. He urged the graduates to uphold Lord Mahavira’s ideals of compassion, humanity and selfless service.
On the occasion, the Vice-President joined the students in taking the “No to Drugs” pledge. He also released the Silver Jubilee commemorative Coffee Table Book.
Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, Director General of Health Services Dr. L. G. Krishna, Director, VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital Dr. Kavita Rani Sharma and Principal Dr. Geetika Khanna were among those present.

date:

content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will participate in the valedictory session of the Departmental Summit on Social Justice and Empowerment on 19 November 2026 at around 4:30 PM at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan, New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.
The two-day Departmental Summit, being held on 18-19 November 2026, will bring together political leadership and officials from States dealing with the sectors of Social Justice and Empowerment and Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities. It is the third in the series of Departmental Summits envisioned by the Prime Minister to strengthen cooperative federalism, foster collective ownership of national priorities and accelerate outcomes through closer Centre-State collaboration.

Reimagining Prevention and Drug demand Reduction Strategy for a Nasha Mukt Bharat.
One Nation One Scholarship portal- Accessible Scholarships, Empowered Students.
Early Intervention and Reduction of Disability Burden
Sugamya Bharat for Viksit Bharat.

content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Annual General Meeting and Annual Convention of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) on 19 November 2026 at around 11 AM at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.
The convention, themed “Bharat 2047”, will bring together over 2,500 delegates, including industry leaders, CEOs, ambassadors, diplomats and policymakers. The year 2026-27 marks FICCI's centenary year, as the organisation completes 100 years of its establishment on 7 April 2027.
Established in 1927, FICCI was founded at a time when Indian enterprises had limited representation in economic policymaking. Since Independence, FICCI has been associated with India's economic transformation and its growing integration with the global economy.
Today, FICCI represents over 2.5 lakh companies across the public, private and multinational sectors, directly and through more than 300 affiliated regional and state-level industry associations. It has partnership agreements with 250 national business associations in over 100 countries.

title: LOK SABHA SPEAKER PARTICIPATES IN VISHWA SHANTI MAHAYAGYA AT HISTORIC SHRI HATKESHWAR MAHADEV TEMPLE IN VADNAGAR
subtitle:
VADNAGAR STANDS AS AN ENDURING SYMBOL OF SPIRITUAL HERITAGE, DETERMINATION, AND SELFLESS PUBLIC SERVICE: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

PRIME MINISTER SHRI MODI’S JOURNEY FROM MODEST ROOTS IN VADNAGAR TO NATIONAL LEADERSHIP EXEMPLIFIES DEDICATION TO PUBLIC SERVICE: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LOK SABHA SPEAKER INTERACTS WITH STUDENTS AND VISITS HISTORIC SCHOOLS, ARCHAEOLOGICAL EXPERIENTIAL MUSEUM, AND MUSEUM OF MUSIC IN VADNAGAR
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 7:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla visited Vadnagar in Mehsana district, Gujarat, today and participated in a series of spiritual, educational, and cultural engagements.
Beginning his visit at the historic Shri Hatkeshwar Mahadev Temple, Shri Birla offered prayers and participated in the ongoing 10-day Vishwa Shanti Mahayagya organised under the divine guidance and presence of Kanchi Kamakoti Peethadhipati Jagadguru Sri Shankara Vijayendra Saraswati Swamigal.
Sharing his reflections after the Mahayagya, the Lok Sabha Speaker described the ancient Hatkeshwar Mahadev Temple as a sacred centre of India’s spiritual heritage that inspires generations. He noted that the Vishwa Shanti Mahayagya and Havan, held under the leadership of Jagadguru Shankaracharya Ji, are dedicated to universal peace, harmony among nations, and the welfare of all humanity and living beings.
Highlighting the significance of Vadnagar as a sacred centre of India’s cultural legacy and the birthplace of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Shri Birla remarked that the historic town stands as an enduring symbol of spiritual heritage, determination, and selfless public service. He said that visiting the town and seeing the Prime Minister’s school and the places associated with his formative years offer deep insight into how extraordinary resolve can triumph over adversity. He observed that the town serves as an inspirational landmark demonstrating that regardless of economic hardship, family struggles, or challenging circumstances, clear goals and unwavering determination enable an individual to achieve their aspirations.
Shri Birla noted that from his early student days, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s life has been defined by a spirit of learning, dialogue, debate, and spiritual inspiration drawn from the ideals of Swami Vivekananda. Driven by the resolve of Seva (service), he left home at a young age to travel across the country, understanding India’s diverse social and economic realities firsthand. Calling this journey a testament to the strength of Indian democracy, the Speaker said that rising from a small town amidst modest circumstances to lead the nation exemplifies how dedication to public service shapes leadership.
Underscoring the Prime Minister’s milestone of 25 years of continuous public service as Chief Minister and Prime Minister, Shri Birla said that this enduring commitment serves as a major source of inspiration for every citizen. Having personally experienced economic and social challenges early in life, the Prime Minister has channelled those insights into building a self-reliant (Atmanirbhar) and self-sustaining India capable of overcoming future challenges, the Speaker added.
Following his engagements at the temple, the Lok Sabha Speaker visited Prerna School in Vadnagar, where he interacted warmly with students, encouraging them to cultivate curiosity, engage in constructive dialogue, and dedicate themselves to nation-building. He also visited Shri B.N. High School, paying tribute to the educational institutions that shaped young minds in the historic town.
Later, Shri Birla visited the Archaeological Experiential Museum and the Museum of Music in Vadnagar, appreciating the rich civilisational, archaeological, and musical legacy of one of India’s oldest living towns.

title: Union Ayush Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav Meets H.E. Mr. Roger Baro, Minister and Special Adviser to the President of Burkina Faso
subtitle:
India Keen to Work Closely with Burkina Faso in Traditional Medicine: Shri Prataprao Jadhav

Institutional Collaboration Will Open New Avenues for Traditional Medicine Cooperation: Shri Jadhav
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 7:02PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, met with the delegation of Burkina Faso led by H.E. Mr. Roger Baro, Minister and Special Adviser to the President of Burkina Faso, in New Delhi today. The Burkinabe delegation is visiting India from 17 to 25 November 2026. The visit focuses on traditional medicine and Ayush institutions.
During the meeting, Shri Prataprao Jadhav said that India attaches great importance to its bilateral relations with Burkina Faso and is keen to further strengthen the partnership. He noted that the two countries share a rich heritage of traditional medicines and indigenous healthcare practices, which provides a strong foundation for cooperation in this field.
Shri Jadhav said he had learnt that the President of Burkina Faso, H.E. Captain Ibrahim Traore, had expressed interest in India’s support for the conservation and sustainable development of Burkina Faso’s traditional medicinal plants. He added that India is keen to work closely with Burkina Faso in the field of traditional medicines and is ready to share its experience and expertise, including in herbal medicine standardisation, quality assurance, pharmacopoeial standards and the regulatory framework.
Shri Jadhav welcomed institutional partnerships between Ayush institutions in India and relevant traditional medicine institutions in Burkina Faso. He noted considerable potential for a flagship India-Burkina Faso Project on Conservation and Sustainable Development of Traditional Plants, in collaboration with India’s National Medicinal Plants Board and relevant institutions in Burkina Faso.
The Minister said India is also keen to support the promotion of Yoga and Ayush-based wellness programmes in Burkina Faso. He said the two sides could explore the possibility of signing a Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Ayush and Burkina Faso’s Ministry of Health to promote an institutional framework. He also welcomed Burkina Faso’s participation in future WHO Global Summits on Traditional Medicine and in programmes at the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre in Jamnagar, Gujarat. As an immediate step, he suggested that both sides identify nodal officers to take the proposal forward and work out specific areas of cooperation.
Highlighting India's commitment to South-South Cooperation and its engagement through G20 and BRICS, the Minister said India offers full support to Burkina Faso in achieving its developmental goals, and that the developmental partnership is guided by the needs and priorities set by the Government of Burkina Faso. He said India is also contributing to capacity building through training and scholarship initiatives under programmes such as ITEC, ICCR and the PCFD course, from which more than 250 Burkinabe nationals have benefited in the last few years.
The Minister noted that the small but vibrant Indian community in Burkina Faso has been making a positive contribution to the country’s socio-economic development. He said that India would appreciate the continued support of the Government of Burkina Faso in ensuring the safety and security of the community. He added that India is committed to working closely with Burkina Faso to promote traditional medicine through cooperation, knowledge exchange and capacity building. Shri Jadhav wished the delegation a successful and productive visit and said he looks forward to taking bilateral cooperation further.
The delegation included Prof. Rakissida Alfred Ouedraogo, Special Ministerial Advisor for Higher Education and Health Issues; Dr. Mariam Sawadogo/Bagayan, Director of Traditional and Alternative Medicine at the Ministry of Health, serving as the mission’s rapporteur; Prof. Aminata Pagnimdebsom Nacoulma, Lecturer-Researcher specialising in Pharmacognosy at Joseph Ki-Zerbo University; and Dr. Hyacinthe Bonkoungou, Specialised Pharmacist and Director of the Center for Traditional Medicine and Integrated Care.
The Burkina Faso Embassy was represented by Mr. Some Désiré Boniface, Ambassador; Mr. Zingué-ouattara Didier Christian, Deputy Chief of Mission; and Mr. Ouoba Joël, interpreter. From the Ministry of External Affairs, the meeting was attended by Shri O. P. Meena, Ambassador of India to Burkina Faso, and Shri Kailash Bhatt, Under Secretary (Central & West Africa), MEA. Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha and senior officials of the Ministry of Ayush were also present at the meeting.
The meeting reaffirmed the shared commitment of India and Burkina Faso to deepen cooperation in traditional medicine and strengthen collaboration between Ayush institutions and their Burkinabe counterparts.

title: Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav Chairs 13th Governing Body Meeting of National Institute of Unani Medicine
subtitle: Shri Jadhav Calls for Timely Action, Accountability and Expansion of Unani Education and Research
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 6:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for the Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State in the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Shri Prataprao Jadhav, today chaired the 13th Governing Body meeting of the National Institute of Unani Medicine (NIUM) at Kartavya Bhawan-I, New Delhi.
Highlighting NIUM's role in advancing Unani education, research and healthcare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav noted that the institute currently has 71 students across 10 postgraduate departments. He highlighted the proposed expansion through five additional postgraduate departments, 35 additional seats and a Department of Integrative and Translational Research.
Shri Jadhav also highlighted the development of NIUM's second campus at Ghaziabad, near Delhi, with a proposed 200-bed referral hospital, postgraduate education and research facilities. Welcoming the proposal for 24 seats for foreign students within the existing intake capacity, he said it would strengthen international academic engagement and reflect the spirit of
Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam (
वसुधैव
कुटुम्बकम्
).
The Minister outlined three key expectations from NIUM — timeliness, accountability and service — stressing that pending matters should be addressed promptly and clear timelines and responsibilities assigned to every project. Union minister emphasised that healthcare services and treatments developed by the institute must reach even the poorest sections of society.
Prof. Saiyad Shah Alam, Director, National Institute of Unani Medicine (NIUM), Bengaluru, welcomed the Union Minister and the Secretary, Ministry of Ayush. He also made a presentation highlighting the institute’s activities, achievements and proposed initiatives.
The meeting was attended by Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha; Additional Secretary and Financial Adviser, Shri Hoyeeda Abbas; Additional Chief Secretary, Department of Finance, Government of Karnataka, Shri Ritesh Kumar Singh; Advisor (Unani), Ministry of Ayush, Dr. M.A. Qasmi; President, Board of Unani, Siddha and Sowa-Rigpa, Prof. Asim Ali Khan; and Director General, Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM), Dr. N. Zaheer Ahmed, among other senior officials.
The meeting concluded with a focus on strengthening institutional governance, ensuring effective implementation of approved initiatives and enhancing coordination among stakeholders for the institute's future development.

Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, conveyed their greetings and best wishes through video messages played during the programme.
In his message, Shri Prataprao Jadhav highlighted the importance of naturopathy in strengthening preventive healthcare and promoting healthy lifestyles.
Shri Jadhav called upon citizens to adopt healthy habits and contribute towards building a Swasth Bharat. He also appreciated the efforts of practitioners, researchers, institutions and other stakeholders in promoting naturopathy and creating greater public awareness about the system.
Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, in his message, emphasised the role of naturopathy in preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyle promotion and fostering harmony with nature. He underlined the importance of scientific research, health awareness and community participation in advancing naturopathy and encouraged citizens to adopt informed and sustainable health practices.
Shri N. Cheluvarayaswamy, Minister for Water Resources (Major and Medium Irrigation), Government of Karnataka and MLA from Nagamangala, attended the programme as the Chief Guest, while Ms. Alarmelmangai D., Joint Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, was the Guest of Honour.
Addressing the gathering, Shri N. Cheluvarayaswamy appreciated the establishment and development of CRIYN, Nagamangala, and highlighted its potential to address the healthcare needs of the region. He emphasised the need to make the institute's facilities accessible to the general public, enabling people in the surrounding areas to benefit from naturopathy-based healthcare services.
He assured his full support and cooperation for the further development of the institute and expressed his willingness to coordinate with the State Government to facilitate the implementation of Ministry of Ayush projects and other Government of India initiatives in Karnataka.
Ms. Alarmelmangai D. highlighted the growing recognition of Yoga and Naturopathy and their relevance in addressing lifestyle-related disorders through preventive and promotive healthcare. She also highlighted the expansion of CCRYN's research infrastructure, including the Central Research Institutes of Yoga and Naturopathy at Nagamangala, Karnataka, and Jhajjar, Haryana, along with its facilities at Rohini, Delhi. She acknowledged the contribution of NIN, Pune, to education, research, training, clinical services and public awareness.
Prof. (Dr.) Jyoti Keswani, Director, CCRYN, in her welcome address, highlighted the significance of Naturopathy Day and the Council's role in advancing research, institutional development and the promotion of Yoga and Naturopathy.
The programme featured the release of several research publications, educational resources and initiatives by CCRYN and NIN, Pune. These included documentary films on CRIYN Nagamangala and Jhajjar, the Indian Journal of Yoga & Naturopathy (Volume 1, Issue 3), a Yoga and Naturopathy book, an Intern Booklet and ReGEN-Beta, a clinical trial on lifestyle interventions for Type 2 Diabetes. NIN, Pune, released Nature Cure 360: A Community Health Initiative towards a Sustainable Healthy Future and The Family Doctor.
A Naturopathy Food Fair and a medicinal plant plantation drive were also organised, highlighting the role of natural resources, healthy lifestyles and nature-based healthcare practices.
Prof. (Dr.) Jyoti Keswani, Director, CCRYN; Prof. (Dr.) Geetha B. Shetty, Director, NIN, Pune; and Dr. Vadiraja H.S., Assistant Director, Central Research Institute of Yoga and Naturopathy, Nagamangala, Ministry of Ayush, were among those present at the programme.
The celebration of the 9th Naturopathy Day reaffirmed the importance of research-backed Yoga and Naturopathy in strengthening preventive and promotive healthcare. Through sustained efforts in research, institutional development, public awareness and community participation, the Ministry of Ayush continues to promote holistic well-being and advance the vision of a healthy India.

title: Strengthening India’s Community Seed Banks (CSBs): DIVERSIFARM-India Maps 652 CSBs and Releases New Capacity-Building Manual
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 7:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India has at least 1,000 community seed banks (CSBs), according to a survey conducted by DIVERSIFARM-India. The project’s digital atlas has already mapped 652 of these community-led institutions, providing an important foundation for understanding, strengthening and supporting India's diverse community seed banks.  The outputs were shared at the National Seminar for the Advancement of CSBs held over two days on 17th and 18th November, 2026 at
NASC, New Delhi.
They include a GIS-based atlas with profiles of CSBs, a policy brief on CSB typologies, a roadmap for CSBs in Odisha, and a new capacity-building manual.
Addressing the event, Ms. May-Elin Stener, Ambassador of the Royal Norwegian Embassy in New Delhi, said  that the Embassy welcomed the project’s extensive mapping and support for community seed banks across India. She added that this project is an important component of the partnership between India and Norway.
Dr Regine Andersen, Research Professor, Fridtjof Nansen Institute (FNI), Norway, also shared several outputs from the three-year collaboration between FNI and MSSRF as the core partners of DIVERSIFARM-India. He said that the digital platform brings together community seed banks working across India and creates awareness about their strengths and collective efforts.
Dr Rengalakshmi R, Executive Director, MSSRF said that CSBs are more than just storehouses. She added that they are a living institution for in-situ conservation that builds farmers' resilience.
DIVERSIFARM-India is a project led by Fridtjof Nansen Institute (FNI) and the M S Swaminathan Research Foundation (MSSRF) that aims to improve food, nutrition, and livelihoods for small farmers by strengthening seed systems through community seed banks.
Six typologies to guide policy, One roadmap to shape the future of CSBs in Odisha
The comprehensive study had identified six CSB typologies based on management structures.Identifying these institutional differences is crucial for targeted and effective policy support.
Another policy brief under the project charts a 10-point roadmap for CSBs in Odisha. It recommends a secretariat under the Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Empowerment, to shape and sustain environments that enable CSBs in the state.
Manual offers practical guide to establishing and sustaining CSBs
A capacity-building manual was also developed based on in-depth case studies conducted in Odisha, the pilot state. Combining technical guidance, organizational approaches and policy relevance, it is a practical guide to establish, manage and sustain CSBs in India.
The manual was released by Dr Trilochan Mohapatra, Chairperson, Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority (PPVFRA) at National Agricultural Science Complex, New Delhi. Noting the PPVFRA’s support for CSBs in his inaugural address, he said now that government support is growing, he is sure that the Community Seed Banks would flourish.
Legal and policy landscape
The DIVERSIFARM-India project also examined the legal and policy landscape in India to better understand the bottlenecks and opportunities for CSBs. The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers Right Act (PPVFRA) and The National Biodiversity Act were identified for their demonstrated potentialin strengthening CSBs.
Padma Shri Dr P. L. Gautam, Former Chairperson, PPVFRA and NBA said that to further benefit farmers, a need to establish a synergy between the two laws emerged in discussions.  He added biodiversity is a common heritage of humankind,  reflecting on the founding principle of the laws.
Dr Devendra Kumar Yadava, Director, ICAR-National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources, and DDG (Crop Science), ICAR, highlighted that community gene banks and national gene banks can be strengthened collaboratively. Echoing his recommendation, Padma Shri Dr PL Gautam also underscored committed funding and capacity building as the need of the hour.

title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan to dedicate India's First Indigenous H5N1 (Clade 2.3.2.1a) Chicken Vaccine to the Nation on 20 November
subtitle: ICAR-NIHSAD Develops Indigenous H5N1 Vaccine to Strengthen Poultry Disease Control
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 9:38AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, will dedicate India’s first indigenous Inactivated H5N1 (Clade 2.3.2.1a) Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) Vaccine for Chickens to the Nation on 20th November, 2026 at ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD), Bhopal. Developed indigenously by ICAR-NIHSAD, Bhopal, the vaccine is the first of its kind in India against the H5N1 HPAI virus of Clade 2.3.2.1a.
Background
Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI), commonly known as bird flu, is a serious disease affecting poultry. Outbreaks can cause nearly 100 per cent mortality among infected birds, leading to major financial losses for poultry farmers due to the large-scale culling of birds and restrictions on trade. The impact is not limited to poultry farms; it can also affect global trade, prices of poultry products and the livelihoods of farmers. Since the first detection of the disease in India in 2006, more than 500 combined outbreaks of H5N1 and H5N8 subtypes have been reported in the country.
A major outbreak of bird flu could reduce India's GDP growth by up to 1.5 per cent, while more than 20 per cent of the country's poultry population could be at risk if the disease spreads without control. The 2006 bird flu outbreak caused estimated direct and indirect losses of Rs. 2,200–3,000 crore. An outbreak in Manipur also resulted in losses equivalent to 0.5 per cent of the state's GDP. The disease is also a public health concern. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), 1,003 human cases of H5N1 avian influenza, including 479 deaths, have been reported across 25 countries, including India, since 2003.
Studies of the virus have shown that the H5N1 strain known as Clade 2.3.2.1a has been responsible for most bird flu outbreaks in chickens. In recent times, infections caused by this strain have also been detected in different animal species, including mammals, along with three human cases. This makes it important to control the spread of this virus to reduce financial losses for poultry farmers and prevent its transmission from chickens to other animals and humans.
At present, no specific commercial vaccine is available against the H5N1 virus of Clade 2.3.2.1a. Therefore, developing an indigenous vaccine is important for India. The vaccine developed by ICAR-NIHSAD aims to address this need by providing protection against Clade 2.3.2.1a H5N1 virus strains circulating in the country.

title: Department of Commerce Amends Guidelines of Four Interventions under Export Promotion Mission to Enhance Support for Exporters
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 1:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Commerce has amended the guidelines of four interventions under the Niryat Disha sub-scheme of Export Promotion Mission (EPM) on 17 November 2026 to enhance support for exporters and broaden participation. These interventions are Market Access Support (MAS), Trade Regulations, Accreditation & Compliance Enablement (TRACE), and Logistics Interventions for Freight and Transport (LIFT).
The MAS intervention aims to strengthen India's export market access through structured support for activities such as Buyer-Seller Meets (BSMs), Reverse Buyer-Seller Meets (RBSMs), trade fairs, exhibitions and other related market access initiatives.
The amended guidelines provide for the following changes:
●
The maximum eligible export turnover for availing airfare reimbursement for participation in Buyer-Seller Meets, trade fairs and trade delegations has been increased from ₹75 lakh in the preceding year to ₹50 crore.
●
Airfare reimbursement has been enhanced to up to 95% for Micro and Small Exporters and up to 80% for other eligible exporters.
●
The mandatory membership period with Export Promotion Councils has been reduced from six months to three months.
The TRACE intervention provides support to MSMEs in meeting internationally recognised quality, safety and technical requirements applicable in overseas markets. The support covers compliance- and quality-related certifications, as well as other mandatory and voluntary conformity-assessment requirements.
Under the amended guidelines, the list of certificates eligible for reimbursement has been expanded from 462 to 600, enabling wider coverage and greater support for MSMEs in meeting international quality, safety and technical requirements.
The LIFT intervention seeks to address geographical disadvantages and logistics gaps faced by MSMEs in low export-intensity areas by providing support to reduce freight and transportation costs arising from locational challenges.
The amended guidelines provide for the following changes:
●
The coverage of low export-intensity districts has been expanded from 13 States/UTs to 34 States/UTs.
●
The categories of eligible ports have been expanded to include Land Customs Stations (LCSs) and Integrated Check Posts (ICPs).
●
Waterways have been added to the existing modes of transport, namely road, rail and air.
●
Air freight support for export shipments has been extended to Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, in addition to the existing coverage of the North Eastern Region.
●
The minimum distance eligibility criterion between the origin and destination ports has been reduced from 200 km to 100 km.
●
Support has been extended to all exportable merchandise items, except those specified in the negative list of export products/categories of exports.
The Union Cabinet approved the EPM on 12 November 2025, with an outlay of ₹25,060 crore for the period FY 2025-26 to FY 2030-31. The Mission aims to strengthen India's export competitiveness through targeted financial and non-financial support, with a particular focus on MSMEs, first-time exporters and under-represented regions.
The Mission operates through two integrated sub-schemes, Niryat Protsahan, which facilitates access to trade finance, and Niryat Disha, which supports market access and addresses non-financial barriers to exports. A total of 11 interventions under the two sub-schemes have been operationalised so far.
The amendments to these interventions under the Export Promotion Mission reflect the Government's continued commitment to strengthening India's export competitiveness by expanding support for exporters' participation in international trade events, facilitating greater access to certification and compliance assistance, and addressing freight and logistics challenges faced by MSMEs, particularly those located in low export-intensity areas.

title: INDIAN NAVY MARKS 50 YEARS OF LONG-RANGE MARITIME RECONNAISSANCE
subtitle: From the Super Constellation to the P-8I, five decades of vigil over the Indian Ocean and beyond
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 11:00AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Indian Navy marks the Golden Jubilee of its Long-Range Maritime Reconnaissance (LRMR) operations on
18 Nov 2026
. The milestone coincides with the 50th anniversary of the commissioning of Indian Naval Air Squadron (INAS) 312, the ‘Albatross’, and commemorates five decades of airborne vigil in support of India’s maritime security.
Following the 1971 war, the need for shore-based maritime patrol aircraft capable of working alongside ships and helicopters led the Navy to assume responsibility for long-range maritime reconnaissance.
On 18 Nov 1976, INAS 312 was commissioned at INS Hansa, Goa, with five Lockheed Super Constellation aircraft transferred from the Indian Air Force.
The induction of the Ilyushin Il-38 in 1977 strengthened the Navy’s maritime reconnaissance and anti-submarine warfare capability. The Tupolev Tu-142M, inducted into INAS 312 in 1988, extended the Navy’s patrol reach across the Indian Ocean Region. The induction of the Boeing P-8I at INS Rajali, Arakkonam, in 2013 marked a further advance, bringing enhanced capabilities in wide-area intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, anti-submarine warfare and maritime strike.
Over the past five decades, the Navy’s LRMR aircraft have supported Operations Cactus, Vijay, Parakram and Sindoor, as well as anti-piracy and search and rescue missions. Today,
P-8I aircraft of INAS 312 at INS Rajali, Arakkonam, and INAS 316 at INS Hansa, Goa,
continue to maintain vigil over the Indian Ocean and beyond, safeguarding India’s maritime interests.
The Golden Jubilee honours generations of naval aviators, mission crews, maintainers and support personnel whose dedication and professionalism have built and sustained this capability over five decades.

subtitle: GST-2 must take Comprehensive View of Climate Action, recognise Implementation Gaps and deliver Solution-oriented Outcomes: Shri Bhupender Yadav
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 8:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Antalya (Türkiye), 18th November, 2026
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, has called for the Second Global Stocktake (GST-2) under the Paris Agreement to be an open, transparent and inclusive process, grounded in the best available science and equity, and delivering balanced outcomes across all aspects of climate action.
Addressing the High-Level Event on the Second Global Stocktake at UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, the Minister said that the GST must take a comprehensive 360-degree view of the Paris Agreement and its implementation, taking stock of both achievements and existing gaps. He emphasised that the process must be guided by the principles of equity, Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC), with developed countries taking the lead in the light of national circumstances.
Shri Yadav highlighted that the Second GST provides an opportunity to assess progress across key areas, including updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), Biennial Transparency Reports, international cooperation under Article 6, the Global Goal on Adaptation and the Just Transition Mechanism. He also stressed the importance of recognising scientific assessments and reports, particularly those emerging from developing countries, alongside IPCC reports.
The Minister emphasised that the GST-2 must examine why, despite progress in climate action, the world remains at risk of crossing the 1.5°C warming threshold in the coming years. He called for solution-oriented outcomes that guide Parties in updating their NDCs and address gaps in the means of implementation, particularly climate finance and technology transfer. He underlined that actual delivery in these areas has fallen far below the obligations and responsibilities of developed countries.
Concluding his address, Shri Yadav expressed India's expectation that the Second Global Stocktake would be conducted successfully and provide a balanced assessment of global climate action and implementation.

title: India calls for Equity, Climate Justice and Fulfilment of Climate Finance Obligations at UNFCCC COP31, at Antalya (Türkiye)
subtitle:
Global South cannot be made to Bear Burden of Historical Emissions in name of ‘Higher Ambition’: Shri Bhupender Yadav

India stresses Equitable Access to Remaining Carbon Budget and firmly anchors Climate Action in CBDR-RC
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 1:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Antalya (Türkiye), 18th November, 2026
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, delivering India's National Statement at the UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, called for climate action rooted in equity, climate justice and the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC). Emphasising the COP31 theme of ‘Dialogue, Consensus and Action’, the Minister said that honest dialogue, equity-based consensus and urgent action must guide global climate efforts.
Highlighting the historical responsibility for climate change, Shri Yadav stated that the planet's warming is the consequence of two centuries of industrialisation and economic growth in some countries, fuelled by unabated greenhouse gas emissions. Expecting the Global South to bear the burden of addressing the consequences of these historical emissions in the name of ‘higher ambition’ is unjustified, he asserted. The Minister underlined that developing countries cannot be asked to choose between climate action and their legitimate right to development, decent living standards, health and education, adding that equitable access to the remaining carbon budget is non-negotiable.
Shri Yadav stressed that COP decisions and their implementation must be firmly grounded in equity and CBDR-RC. He called for the Mitigation Work Programme (MWP) to remain facilitative and non-prescriptive, the Global Stocktake (GST) to continue serving as an instrument for informing Parties, and the Just Transition Mechanism (JTM) to be anchored in equity. The Minister also cautioned against unilateral trade measures that penalise developing countries under the guise of climate action and called upon developed countries to honestly and expeditiously fulfil their climate finance obligations.
Highlighting India's climate commitments under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Shri Yadav said that India's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) are aligned with the vision of achieving ‘Viksit Bharat’ by 2047 in a sustainable manner. He also emphasised the need to account for climatic and demographic changes and technological advancements while shaping contemporary cooperation. Stressing that the success of COP31 must be assessed through tangible implementation, the delivery of resources to those who need them and the scaling up of proven solutions, Shri Yadav called for dialogue to build trust, consensus to uphold equity and action to deliver climate justice.

title: DRI seizes 148 kg alprazolam intermediate and over 1,046 kg raw materials and chemicals in clandestine drug manufacturing laboratory bust in Delhi; one arrested
subtitle: Illicit laboratory operating under the guise of a computer shop unearthed in Ghazipur, New Delhi; Officials dismantle complete manufacturing setup
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 2:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant crackdown on clandestine manufacturing of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in India, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), busted an illicit laboratory manufacturing Alprazolam at Ghazipur, New Delhi, during 15–16 November 2026.
In an intelligence led operation, DRI officers searched a premises which was deceptively operating under the façade of a computer shop. The search revealed a fully functional clandestine laboratory equipped with reaction apparatus, a water chiller, a vacuum exhaust machine and other equipment used in the manufacturing process.
The operation resulted in the recovery of
148 kg Alprazolam intermediate in solid and liquid form
, along with approximately
1,046 kg raw materials and chemicals and 188 litres additional chemicals/liquids
used in the manufacturing process. The laboratory equipment and associated materials were also seized under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.
The person operating the clandestine laboratory was arrested under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985.
Alprazolam is a benzodiazepine-class psychotropic substance, commonly marketed under brand names such as Xanax, Alprax etc. It is a prescription medicine used primarily for the treatment of anxiety and panic disorders. However, its misuse, dependence potential and diversion into illicit channels pose significant public health concerns. Alprazolam is a notified psychotropic substance under the NDPS Act, 1985, and its unauthorised manufacture, possession, sale and distribution attract penal provisions of the Act.
This operation follows DRI's recent busting of a major clandestine synthetic drug manufacturing laboratory in Jalaun district, Uttar Pradesh, on 29 October 2026, with operational assistance from UP ATS. The operation had resulted in the seizure of approximately 1,100 kg of drugs and precursor chemicals, along with manufacturing equipment, and the arrest of two persons.
The busting of the clandestine laboratory in Delhi within weeks of the Jalaun operation underscores DRI's intensified focus on identifying and dismantling illicit drug manufacturing facilities, removing substantial quantities of intermediate materials and precursor chemicals from the illicit supply chain, and disrupting the networks sustaining such operations.

Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, addressed the 8th Convocation Ceremony of Vardhman Mahavir Medical College (VMMC) and Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi, today, in the presence of Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare, Shri J. P. Nadda. The convocation was organised as part of the institution’s Silver Jubilee Year celebrations, marking 25 years of its establishment (2001–2026).
Addressing the gathering, Vice President, Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan, the Hon’ble Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, congratulated Vardhman Mahavir Medical College (VMMC) and Safdarjung Hospital on completing 25 years of dedicated service in medical education and healthcare delivery. He observed that the institution continues to serve as a vital pillar of the country’s public healthcare system, making significant contributions to medical education, patient care and the development of healthcare professionals. Highlighting the progress made in the healthcare sector under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he noted that the country has witnessed substantial expansion of its healthcare infrastructure, including the establishment of 12 new AIIMS over the past 12 years.
Reflecting on the responsibilities that accompany the medical profession, the Vice President emphasised that a medical degree is not merely an academic qualification but a lifelong commitment to humanity. He reminded the graduating students that despite remarkable advancements in medical science and technology, the human touch and compassionate relationship between a doctor and a patient remain irreplaceable. He urged them to uphold the highest standards of professional ethics and ensure that every patient is treated with dignity, compassion and respect, irrespective of their financial circumstances or social background. He underscored that there must be no discrimination in the delivery of healthcare and that every individual deserves equal and humane treatment.
Referring to the national vision articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice President highlighted the goal of building a Viksit Bharat by 2047. He observed that the vision of a developed India cannot be realised without a healthy India, making a strong and equitable healthcare system indispensable to the country's overall development. He called upon the graduating doctors to recognise their important role in advancing this national aspiration through their professional commitment and service to society.
Addressing the young graduates, the Vice President observed that among the country's 140 crore citizens, doctors occupy a uniquely respected position because of the trust and responsibility associated with their profession. He encouraged them to regard this respect as both a privilege and a responsibility, always placing the nation above personal considerations and remaining committed to the welfare of society. He also urged the graduating students to say no to drugs, promote awareness against substance abuse and actively encourage others to lead healthy and responsible lives.
Speaking at the Occasion, Shri J.P. Nadda, described the occasion as a momentous milestone, symbolising years of dedication, academic excellence and commitment to service. Congratulating the students on successfully completing their medical education, he observed that graduating from Vardhman Mahavir Medical College was a matter of great distinction, given the exceptional clinical exposure, diverse learning opportunities and professional experience that the institution offers. He emphasised that while education is a fundamental right, the opportunity to enter the medical profession is a privilege that entails a profound responsibility towards society. He urged the graduates to discharge this responsibility with dedication, compassion and integrity, and to place their professional knowledge and skills at the service of humanity.
Highlighting the remarkable transformation of India's medical education landscape under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Shri Nadda noted that the country has made significant strides in expanding both medical education infrastructure and institutional capacity. He observed that India, which had only one AIIMS by the end of the 20th century, now has 23 AIIMS. Similarly, the number of medical colleges has increased from 387 to 863, with plans to establish 75,000 additional medical colleges over the next five years.
Referring to the Prime Minister's announcement from the ramparts of the Red Fort regarding the expansion of medical education capacity, Shri Nadda reiterated the Government's commitment to creating 75,000 additional medical seats. He expressed confidence that this target would be realised by 2029. Underscoring the scale of expansion achieved over the past decade, he stated that undergraduate medical seats have increased from approximately 51,000 to 1.43 lakh, while postgraduate seats have risen from around 31,000 to 91,000.
Emphasising that the expansion of medical education has been accompanied by an equally strong focus on maintaining academic and institutional standards, Shri Nadda stated that the Government remains committed to ensuring that increased capacity does not come at the cost of quality. He further informed that the Union Cabinet, in December 2025, approved financial assistance of ₹1.5 crore for each additional undergraduate and postgraduate medical seat, with an overall allocation of ₹15,000 crore to facilitate the creation of 10,000 additional medical seats.
Concluding his address, Shri Nadda reminded the graduating students that their achievements were not solely the outcome of their individual efforts but also reflected the sacrifices, encouragement and support of their parents, families and the larger society. He urged them to remain conscious of this collective contribution and to give back to society through selfless service, professional excellence and a steadfast commitment to their responsibilities as healthcare professionals.
Welcoming the Dignitaries, Dr. Kavita Rani Sharma, Director, VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital, extended her gratitude to the dignitaries and highlighted the institution’s remarkable journey of 25 years in medical education and healthcare delivery. She described the institution as a representation of the harmonious integration of medical science and healthcare, with education and service continuing to remain at the core of its institutional ethos. Emphasising the values that define the medical profession, she urged the graduating students to uphold the highest standards of integrity, honesty and ethical conduct, and to discharge their professional responsibilities with dedication, compassion and a strong commitment to patient care.
During the ceremony, the Hon’ble Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, released the Annual Report and Silver Jubilee Commemorative Volume of VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital. Furthermore, Vice President Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan led the pledge on “No to Drugs”, reinforcing the message of a drug-free society.
This was followed by the presentation of the Academic Report by Dr. (Prof.) Geetika Khanna, Principal, VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital, highlighting the institution’s achievements and progress in medical education, healthcare delivery and research.
A total of 423 students received their degrees during the ceremony, including 265 postgraduate and super speciality students and 158 undergraduate students. In recognition of their academic excellence, 46 meritorious students, comprising 29 postgraduate/super speciality and 17 undergraduate students, were awarded medals.
VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital Marks 25 Years
Established in 2001, Vardhman Mahavir Medical College and Safdarjung Hospital has completed 25 years of contribution to medical education, healthcare delivery and research. Over the years, the institution has played an important role in medical education and the development of healthcare professionals, while strengthening its academic and clinical capabilities.
The 8th Convocation, held during the Silver Jubilee Year, celebrates the achievements of graduating students and marks an important milestone in the institution’s continued commitment to excellence in medical education, research and patient care.
The occasion brought together Senior Officials of the Ministry, faculty members, graduating students and distinguished guests to celebrate the academic achievements of the graduating batch and commemorate the institution's 25 years of service in the field of medical education and healthcare.
Dr Loveneesh G. Krishna, Director General Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; Dr. Kavita Rani Sharma, Director, VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital, Dr. Geetika Khanna, Principal, VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital were also present at the event.

title: Union Health Ministry Observes World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week 2026, Calls for Collective Action against AMR
subtitle:
Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava Emphasises One Health Approach under This Year's Theme, ‘One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now’

Smt. Srivastava Urges Responsible Antimicrobial Use and Stronger Infection Prevention Practices to Contain AMR
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 6:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, today, inaugurated the national observance of the World Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) Awareness Week 2026 at Kartavya Bhawan, New Delhi. The week-long observance is significant as it seeks to build greater awareness and collective action against antimicrobial resistance, one of the most urgent threats to public health.
Addressing the event virtually, Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava drew attention to the growing threat of Antimicrobial Resistance, describing it as one of the most serious public health challenges of our time. She noted that medicines that have saved countless lives are gradually losing their effectiveness due to misuse and overuse. She cautioned that if left unchecked, AMR could undermine decades of medical progress, making even common infections difficult to treat and posing a serious threat to human health.
Referring to this year's theme,
‘
One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now
’
, Smt. Srivastava underscored the need for coordinated action across sectors. Drawing attention to the vision of the Hon
’
ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, she stressed on the importance of adopting a One Health approach that recognises the interconnectedness of human health, animal health, plant and food systems and the environment. She noted that the improper use of antimicrobials across these sectors contributes to the emergence and spread of resistance, underscoring the need for coordinated action to address this growing threat.
The Union Health Secretary highlighted that the Government of India has accorded high priority to AMR containment. She said that the
National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance 2.0 (NAP AMR 2.0), 2025–2029
, launched by Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda during World AMR Awareness Week in November 2025, provides a comprehensive framework for surveillance, infection prevention, responsible antimicrobial use, research and coordinated action across sectors.
She also highlighted the efforts being undertaken by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare through the National Programme on AMR Containment, coordinated by the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), which focuses on strengthening laboratory capacity for AMR surveillance, infection prevention and control, antimicrobial stewardship and awareness generation.
Highlighting the role of healthcare professionals, Smt. Srivastava stressed that antibiotics should be prescribed only when clinically indicated and in accordance with appropriate treatment guidelines. She also underscored the responsibility of pharmacists in ensuring appropriate dispensing of antimicrobials against valid prescriptions and counselling patients on their correct use.
Urging the public to adopt responsible practices, she advised against self-medication, sharing antibiotics or using leftover medicines. She reminded citizens that antibiotics are not effective against viral infections such as the common cold and influenza. She also highlighted the importance of hygiene and sanitation, safe water, safe food and vaccination in preventing infections, thereby reducing the need for antibiotic use.
Smt. Srivastava concluded her address by encouraging States and Union Territories, healthcare institutions, educational institutions and community organisations to take the message of AMR awareness to every section of society. She emphasised that the commitment to combat antimicrobial resistance must extend beyond the awareness week, with its success reflected in everyday practices relating to the prescription, dispensing and use of antimicrobials, and effective infection prevention. Calling for collective action, she urged all stakeholders to work together to preserve the effectiveness of essential antimicrobial medicines and safeguard the health of present and future generations.
The meeting participants, which included representatives of various stakeholder organisations, took note of the fact that more than half of antimicrobial sales in India occur without prescriptions, while nearly half of outpatient antibiotic prescriptions are inappropriate. They underscored the urgent need to address these practices and identified several measures that could be scaled up across the country. These include public awareness campaigns; preventing self-prescription of antibiotics; proper disposal of antibiotics and expired medicines; displaying legal warnings at drug shops against the sale of antimicrobials without prescriptions; curbing the production of substandard and spurious medicines; promoting the appropriate use of antibiotics in veterinary medicine, particularly for food-producing animals; and maintaining quality standards in healthcare facilities to prevent the occurrence and spread of infections.
The event was attended by senior officers from the National Health Systems Resource Centre (NHSRC), Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), Department of Animal Husbandry, Indian Medical Association and All India Association of Druggists and Chemists. Senior officers from States and Union Territories also attended the event virtually.
About World Anti Microbial Resistance Awareness Week
World AMR Awareness Week is a global campaign celebrated from 18th to 24th November every year to improve awareness and understanding of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and encourage best practices among the public, One Health stakeholders and policymakers. All these stakeholders play a critical role in reducing the further emergence and spread of AMR.

ICMR marks 115 years of service to the nation; 17 indigenous health technologies showcased
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 12:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has achieved the milestone of 100 successful technology transfers deals, marking a significant step in translating indigenous health research into technologies and solutions for wider public use. The milestone was announced at the 3rd Department of Health Research (DHR)-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit, which concluded today at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.
Organised by DHR and ICMR on 16 and 17 November 2026, the two-day Summit brought together over 600 scientists, researchers, innovators, administrators and policymakers from ICMR institutes, partner institutions, government organisations and academia. The Summit also marked 115 years of ICMR's contribution to biomedical and health research in the country.
The Summit serves as a national platform for recognising excellence in health research and promoting the translation of scientific evidence into tangible outcomes. It showcases significant contributions from ICMR institutes and extramural partner institutions across research publications, technologies, patents and research management, while facilitating collaboration among researchers, industry and policymakers.
At the Technology Transfer Ceremony, ICMR exchanged 20 licensing agreements covering eight technologies with nine Indian companies, taking the cumulative number of successful technology transfers deals to 100 within limited time of less than 2 years of Medical Innovations Patent Mitra, an flagship initiative of ICMR launched by Union Health and Family Welfare Minister, Shri J P Nadda in March, 2025. This milestone reflects ICMR's continued efforts to facilitate the translation of research and indigenous innovations into practical applications through industry partnerships.
An Innovation Exhibition showcased 17 technologies developed by ICMR institutes and extramural partner institutions. In addition, 10 technologies and eight patents were presented during a dedicated session on Technologies and Patents, highlighting the breadth of innovation emerging from the country's health research ecosystem.
Three new initiatives were launched at the Summit. The DHR’s new Research to Action Vertical will translate research evidence into decision-ready products for policy and programmes. Syndromic Surveillance under the DHR Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDL) Scheme will create an early-warning network for outbreaks across 70 VRDLs and Infectious Disease Research & Diagnostic Laboratories (IRDLs). The Dr M K Bhan Young Medical Faculty PhD Portal launched today will serve as a centralised digital platform with information for prospective applicants.
ICMR also released the Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) Annual Report and Standard Operating Procedures, bringing together the national evidence base on antimicrobial resistance and standardised laboratory procedures. The ICMR Compendium, featuring 25 stories of research translated into outcomes for people, was also released.
The Research Excellence Showcase presented shortlisted publications, while the Innovation Excellence Showcase featured shortlisted technologies and patents. A dedicated track on research administration and finance deliberated on measures to streamline grant management, procurement and financial processes. A special session commemorated the Golden Jubilee of the ICMR-National Institute of Malaria Research (ICMR-NIMR), marking 50 years of its contribution to malaria research.
The Summit also recognised outstanding contributions across the health research ecosystem through the Research, Innovation and Institutional Excellence Recognition. Researchers and institutions were recognised across nine categories for achievements in publications, technologies, patents and institutional performance. The ICMR Research Management Excellence Recognition acknowledged the contributions of reviewers involved in project selection, the Indian Journal of Medical Research, scientific divisions, scientific support units, and administration and finance teams in strengthening the research ecosystem and supporting high-quality research.
The top 100 school students selected through the SHINE National Competition were also recognised at the Summit for their contributions and scientific thinking in public health. SHINE (Science and Health Innovation for the NextGen Explorers) is a nationwide ICMR initiative for students in Grades 9 to 12 from government, government-aided and private schools across the country. The initiative seeks to foster scientific temper, encourage curiosity and inspire young students to explore careers in biomedical and health research.
The Summit reaffirmed the importance of a strong, collaborative and innovation-driven health research ecosystem in addressing national health priorities and advancing India's pursuit of accessible, affordable and quality healthcare.
The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), headquartered in New Delhi, is the apex body in India for the formulation, coordination and promotion of biomedical research. Established in 1911, ICMR is one of the oldest medical research organisations in the world and functions under the Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India.

subtitle:

Conference to serve as a platform for collective deliberation among security agencies, investigators and experts on emerging terror threats

The conference places particular emphasis on fostering synergy among all stakeholders with the 'Whole of Government approach'

content:
In line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s policy of Zero Tolerance against terrorism,
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah will inaugurate the two-day 'Anti-Terror Conference' in New Delhi on Thursday, 19th November 2026. The conference is being organised by the National Investigation Agency (NIA), Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, as a part of a continued effort to bolster the nation's collective response to terrorism. This year's conference will deliberate on the theme 'Cross-Border Terrorism'.
Held annually, the conference has steadily grown into a significant gathering of operational forces, agencies working in the field of counter-terrorism, and experts from the technical, legal and forensic domains. It offers the agencies / forces, an opportunity to collectively examine matters that have bearing on national security and the threats arising from terrorism.
In keeping with the 'Whole of Government approach', the conference places particular emphasis on fostering synergy among all stakeholders. It seeks to establish formal as well as informal channels that enable coordinated and concerted action against terrorism. The conference also aims at contributing substantive inputs towards the formulation of future policy.
The conference sessions will address a range of subjects, including, obtaining evidence from foreign jurisdictions, the application of digital forensics and data analysis in counter-terrorism investigations, and the effective management of trials. Sessions will also cover countering radicalisation, and emerging hybrid threats to national security. Further sessions will examine the tools, techniques and case experiences involved in disrupting terror financing networks, as well as the development of future-ready counter-terrorism strategies and the strengthening of institutional capacities to meet emerging national security challenges.
This year, the conference will also host a capacity-building training programme for State police personnel and practising professionals. The programme has been designed to equip participants in several areas. These include applying the new criminal laws in terror investigations, using digital evidence in prosecution, and trial strategy and management. The programme will also cover special provisions relating to the investigation of terror cases, common challenges posed by the defence, the protection of witnesses, and the initiatives taken by the Government to improve prosecution.
Over the two days, the deliberations will enable law enforcement agencies to share their experiences, highlight good practices in handling counter-terrorism matters, and draw upon lessons learnt from terror investigations.
The conference will be attended by senior police officers of States and Union Territories, officers of Central agencies and departments dealing with counter-terrorism, and experts from allied fields including law, forensics and technology.
