title: Parvat Manthan Conclave 2026 concludes with recommendations to strengthen climate resilience, ecological planning and municipal finance in Himalayan cities
subtitle:
Two-day Regional Conclave brings together representatives from 11 Himalayan states to address integrated water and sanitation management, climate resilience and ecosystem-based urban development

Ten initiatives, publications and learning resources launched; 18 innovative urban solutions recognised under अrban Learnathon 2.0
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 6:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Parvat Manthan Conclave 2026, convened by the National Institute of Urban Affairs (NIUA), concluded today in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, with recommendations to strengthen urban resilience, ecological planning and sustainable service delivery across the Indian Himalayan Region. The two-day Conclave, held from 17 to 18 November 2026, brought together policymakers, representatives from Himalayan states, urban local bodies, technical experts, academia, civil society organisations and development partners to deliberate on the distinct challenges of mountain urbanisation and identify practical approaches for resilient and sustainable urban development.
The Conclave was inaugurated on 17 November 2026 by Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India, under the theme
‘From Water Security to Ecosystem-Based Urban Development: Mainstreaming Resilient Water and Sanitation for Himalayan Cities’
.
Delivering the inaugural address, Shri Tokhan Sahu
emphasised the importance of regional cooperation, institutional capacity building and knowledge-sharing in addressing the challenges faced by Himalayan cities. Stating that “by pooling knowledge, strengthening local capacities and learning from each other, we can advance solutions for water security, inclusive urban services and dignified sanitation, recognising that challenges do not stop at geographical boundaries”, he called for stronger collaboration among governments, institutions and regional stakeholders. Highlighting the importance of replicating successful urban innovations, he observed that “a solution confined to one city benefits only that city, but a solution shared and replicated has the potential to transform a hundred cities”.
Shri Nitesh Jha, Secretary, Urban Development, Government of Uttarakhand noted that as the source of the Ganga, the Yamuna and other major rivers, Uttarakhand bears a responsibility to every town and village downstream. For this reason, he said, the state treats the management of used water and faecal sludge as a commitment rather than a municipal chore. Tracing the state-led partnership with NIUA since 2019, he highlighted the Septage Management Protocol of 2017 and the co-treatment of septage at existing sewage treatment plants in Ganga towns. He also cited Rudrapur’s faecal sludge treatment plant, the first standalone facility in the state, which was built with support from NIUA. He called on partners, Union ministries and hill states to help design norms and financing that recognise the realities of mountain terrain.
Ms Nameeta Prasad, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), described the Himalayan region as the water tower of Asia, observing that its water crisis stems not from scarcity but from declining springs, pollution, inadequate infrastructure and growing urban demand. Emphasising that Himalayan cities cannot be water secure unless their surrounding ecosystems are healthy, she called for water security to be addressed within a wider ecological framework rather than through centralised infrastructure alone. She highlighted the National Mission on Himalayan Studies (NMHS) as a key platform in this effort, noting that it has supported over 255 projects, including more than 40 on water resource management.
Prof. (Dr) Debolina Kundu, Director, NIUA
, highlighted the evolution of Parvat Manthan into a community of practice that brings together mountain states, institutions and regional partners to exchange knowledge, strengthen capacities and develop practical solutions. She noted that the platform has facilitated peer learning, regional cooperation and policy dialogue to support more responsive approaches to the unique challenges of mountain urbanisation.
Shri Vinod Goswami, Director, Urban Development Department, Government of Uttarakhand
, emphasised the need for long-term, integrated and regionally coordinated planning. He observed that urbanisation must be understood beyond municipal boundaries, recognising its implications for surrounding rural areas and the wider region. He also highlighted the importance of strengthening the financial sustainability of urban local bodies by effectively utilising available resources and financing opportunities, including the 16th Finance Commission and the Urban Challenge Fund.
Key Areas of Technical Deliberation
The Conclave featured four technical sessions examining disaster resilience, integrated water management, ecological carrying capacity and municipal finance, with a focus on strengthening sustainable urban development in the Indian Himalayan Region.
Session 1: Living on the Edge: Disaster Risk, Fragility, and the Future of Hill Infrastructure
The session examined the vulnerability of Himalayan settlements to natural disasters, climate-related risks and increasing infrastructure pressures. Discussions focused on the need to integrate disaster risk assessments into urban planning, strengthen the resilience of critical infrastructure, adopt development practices suited to fragile mountain environments and improve institutional preparedness for climate-related and geological hazards.
Session 2: Water Beyond Boundaries: Integrated Water Management for Ecosystem Health in Hill Cities
The session focused on the need for integrated water resource management that extends beyond municipal boundaries and recognises the interdependence of urban settlements, watersheds and surrounding ecosystems. Discussions highlighted source sustainability, watershed conservation, integrated water and sanitation planning, improved coordination among institutions and the importance of ecosystem-based approaches to long-term water security.
Session 3: Within Limits: Carrying Capacity and Biodiversity in Hill City Planning
The session recommended institutionalising carrying capacity assessments within statutory master plans, establishing common planning parameters across Himalayan states and integrating water availability, biodiversity conservation and ecological sensitivity into land-use planning. Discussions emphasised regional planning beyond municipal boundaries, transparent environmental monitoring, sustainable mobility and construction practices appropriate to fragile mountain environments.
Session 4: Strengthening Municipal Finance for Sustainable Service Delivery in Hilly Regions
The session recommended predictable fiscal transfers, differentiated infrastructure costing for hill cities, lifecycle financing and stronger municipal own-source revenues. Discussions highlighted tourism-linked revenue instruments, cluster-based planning, project aggregation, institutional capacity building and greater transparency in municipal budgets, accounts and audits to strengthen financial sustainability and service delivery.
Launches and Releases
The inaugural session witnessed the launch of
ten initiatives, publications and learning resources
focused on sustainable urban development, water and sanitation management, climate resilience, inclusive service delivery and institutional capacity building.
Carrying Capacity Assessment of Haridwar: A Ganga Town in Uttarakhand
The report examines the implications of tourism and population pressures on urban infrastructure and services, offering recommendations for sustainable land-use planning, resource management and urban development.
Roadmap for Transitioning Towards Integrated Citywide Sanitation for Darjeeling Municipality
The report presents a phased approach for strengthening water supply, wastewater management, solid waste management and drainage through integrated planning suited to the geographical and environmental conditions of hill towns.
Built for All: Let's Talk GEDSI in Sanitation
An interactive comic highlighting the importance of gender equity, disability and social inclusion in the planning and delivery of safe, accessible and dignified sanitation services.
Four Seasons, One City: A Year of Climate Change
A story illustrating the impacts of climate-related disasters on urban water and sanitation systems, highlighting practical measures for improving community preparedness and infrastructure resilience.
Himalayan Resilience: Darjeeling – Beyond Postcard
A coffee table book documenting the water, sanitation and waste management challenges experienced in Darjeeling, alongside community initiatives and priorities for sustainable urban development.
Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) E-course
Launched on the National Urban Learning Platform (NULP), the course provides urban officials and sanitation practitioners with practical knowledge to improve workplace safety and promote dignified working conditions for sanitation workers.
Gender, Equity, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) E-course
Launched on NULP, the course supports urban planners, engineers and government officials in incorporating equity, accessibility and inclusion into sanitation infrastructure planning and service delivery.
Water and Sanitation: Sustainable and Resilient Urban Futures E-course
Launched on NULP, the course provides guidance on climate risk assessment, flood and drought preparedness, and the development of resilient and inclusive urban water and sanitation systems.
Training Manual on GIS-based Spatial Mapping for Water and Sanitation Infrastructure Integrating Kobo Toolbox
The manual provides practical guidance on geotagged field data collection, spatial analysis using QGIS and the preparation of maps to support evidence-based water and sanitation planning.
Himalayan Urban Bio-Sheds (HUBS) Initiative for Advancing Ecosystem-based Urban Development
Undertaken by NIUA with support from the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and the National Mission on Himalayan Studies (NMHS), in partnership with the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), the initiative seeks to integrate water, waste, biodiversity and ecosystem health into a unified urban planning framework. Planned for pilot implementation in three towns across Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Sikkim, HUBS aims to promote urban development approaches that respect ecological boundaries while strengthening essential urban services.
अ
rban Learnathon 2.0: Recognition of Innovative Urban Solutions
The inaugural session also marked the announcement of the results of
अ
rban Learnathon 2.0
, with the awardees felicitated by Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs.
Launched on 08 January 2025 during the Capacity for Change Conclave 2025 by Shri Manohar Lal, Hon’ble Union Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs, अrban Learnathon 2.0 was designed to identify and recognise innovative solutions to urban challenges. The initiative received 201 entries, of which 84 were shortlisted and 18 solutions were selected for awards across categories covering government bodies, academia, industry and special mentions.
The second edition expanded participation to academia and industry, recognising the importance of collaboration among urban local bodies, research institutions and enterprises in developing innovative and replicable urban solutions. The results are available on the National Urban Learning Platform at
https://nulp.niua.org/
.
Delivering the closing remarks, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Mishra, Chief Advisor, NIUA
, observed that institutional capacity had emerged as a common concern across the Conclave's four technical sessions. He highlighted the importance of genuine decentralisation, integrated planning, sustainable infrastructure financing and recognising the ecological sensitivity of Himalayan settlements. He emphasised that technical studies and knowledge products, including carrying capacity assessments prepared by NIUA, must inform policies, programmes and implementation practices.
Shri Vinod Kumar, Assistant Director, Urban Development Department, Government of Uttarakhand
, acknowledged the contributions of NIUA and participating institutions towards strengthening regional cooperation on mountain urbanisation. Highlighting the distinct development challenges of Himalayan settlements, he called for continued collaboration among states, innovation and the adoption of technologies appropriate to mountain environments. He stated, “May the spirit of Parvat Manthan inspire us to deepen cooperation among the Himalayan states, encourage innovation and promote the adoption of appropriate technologies for mountain settlements. Our ultimate objective must be to ensure prosperity and a better quality of life for the people living in these regions.”
Dr Mahreen Matto, Team Lead, NIUA,
acknowledged the long-standing partnership of the Government of Uttarakhand and the participation of representatives from 11 Himalayan states. She emphasised the importance of continued collaboration in translating the Conclave's deliberations into actionable knowledge and institutional learning. Stating that “we will ensure that the deliberations of this conclave are carried forward into our forthcoming knowledge products and reports”, she informed participants that the outcomes would be documented and shared for their suggestions and feedback.
The recommendations emerging from the two-day Parvat Manthan Conclave 2026 will inform subsequent efforts to strengthen sustainable urban development across the Indian Himalayan Region.
About Parvat Manthan
Launched by NIUA in 2023, the Parvat Manthan Hill Forum is a regional platform for dialogue, knowledge exchange and collaboration on sustainable mountain urbanisation. Building on earlier editions that addressed decentralised water and sanitation services, waste management and sustainable settlements, Parvat Manthan Conclave 2026 expanded the discussions to include disaster resilience, ecological carrying capacity, biodiversity conservation and long-term infrastructure financing, with the objective of supporting sustainable and resilient urban development in the Indian Himalayan Region.

title: Five Web Series Nominated for Best Web Series Award at IFFI 2026
subtitle: Diverse narratives spanning education, folklore, entrepreneurship, politics and human relationships celebrate the creative potential of India's OTT industry
content:
Goa, 18 November 2026
The evolving landscape of India's digital entertainment industry will take centre stage at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) scheduled to be held in Goa
from 20th to 28th November 2026
with five distinctive web series nominated for the Best Web Series Award under the OTT Awards category. Bringing together stories rooted in social realities, cultural traditions, historical milestones and human relationships, the nominations reflect the diversity and creative ambition of India's growing OTT ecosystem.
Have a look at the nominations
Adarsh Baal Vidyalaya
Adarsh Baal Vidyalaya directed by Himank Gaur brings humour and social commentary to the realities of India's public education system. Set in a government school in Delhi, the series follows headmaster Gyaneshwar Tripathi, whose dream of visiting Cambridge depends on his students performing exceptionally well in their examinations. With disengaged students, institutional shortcomings and a challenging academic environment standing in his way, the arrival of an idealistic teacher sparks an effort to transform the school.
Blending comedy with a reflection on the challenges of education, the series highlights the role of dedicated teachers and the potential for change within public institutions.
Devkhel
Drawing inspiration from folklore and traditional beliefs, Devkhel directed by Chandrakant Lata Gaikwad takes viewers into the mysterious world of Devtali village, where a death occurs every year on the night of Holi. The villagers attribute the recurring incidents to Shankasur, a mythical demon associated with local traditions. When another mysterious death occurs, Inspector Vishwas sets out to uncover the truth behind the disturbing pattern. As the investigation unfolds, village secrets, hidden motives and questions of faith come to the surface.
Blending elements of crime, suspense and folklore, the series explores the delicate intersection of superstition, tradition and reality.
Made in India: A Titan Story
Directed by Robbie Grewal, Made in India: A Titan Story traces the entrepreneurial vision behind the creation of one of India's most recognised homegrown brands. Set in the pre-liberalisation era, the series follows Xerxes Desai and his ambitious endeavour to establish a world-class Indian watch brand in a market dominated by foreign products and smuggled watches. With the guidance of J.R.D. Tata and the support of a committed team, Desai navigates bureaucratic hurdles, financial constraints and technological challenges.
The narrative captures the determination, innovation and pioneering spirit that transformed an ambitious industrial vision into a landmark chapter in India's corporate history.
Mayasabha: The Rise of the Titans
Set against the politically charged landscape of 1970s Andhra Pradesh, Mayasabha: The Rise of the Titans directed by Deva Katta explores the journey of Kakarla Krishnama Naidu (KKN) an idealistic student leader and M.S. Rami Reddy, a young man from a powerful family.
Beginning as close friends despite their different backgrounds, united by their aspirations to bring about social and political change, their relationship gradually comes under strain as they navigate the harsh realities of political life including caste division, money, corruption, power struggle and changing dynamics. Their transformation from comrades to political rivals forms the heart of the narrative, offering a compelling exploration of political manoeuvring, shifting loyalties and the complexities of human relationships within the corridors of power.
Musafir Café
Taking a more intimate approach to storytelling, Musafir Café directed by Ruchir Arun explores the many dimensions of love, companionship and self-discovery. Centred on Chander Mohan Sharma and his relationships with Sudha and Preeti, the series follows his emotional journey through changing circumstances, personal choices and the complexities of human connections. Set against the picturesque landscapes of Bhopal and Mussoorie, the narrative reflects on love, missed opportunities, acceptance and the unexpected turns that shape one's life. It presents relationships as journeys of growth and discovery, where every encounter leaves an imprint on the human experience.
Together, the five nominations showcase the expanding creative possibilities of India's OTT landscape, where stories from different regions, cultures and social contexts find expression through the digital medium. From the challenges of a government classroom and the mysteries of village folklore to India's entrepreneurial journey, political rivalries and the nuances of love, the nominated series demonstrate the range of subjects that contemporary Indian storytelling continues to explore.
The Best Web Series (OTT) Award at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), scheduled to be held in Goa from November 20 to 28, 2026, recognises excellence in original web-based content and celebrates the creative vision and contributions of writers, directors, creators, actors and production teams shaping India's digital entertainment industry. The nominations reaffirm the growing significance of OTT platforms as an important medium for innovative storytelling and cinematic expression.

title: 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) Showcases the Richness of Indian Cinema Alongside ‘Mission Life’
content:
Goa, November 18, 2026
The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), scheduled to be held in Goa from 20th to 28th November 2026 under the overarching theme "Stories Without Borders", places Indian Cinema and the curated Mission Life section at the forefront of global cinematic dialogue. The primary objective of bringing these two pillars together is to celebrate India’s linguistic and regional storytelling diversity while simultaneously using cinema as a catalyst to explore ecological transformations, nature’s agency and sustainable coexistence beyond a purely human-centred perspective.
Through this convergence, the festival seeks to advance the national vision of ‘Create in India for the World’, nurture emerging creative talent, and inspire audiences to reflect on humanity’s shared responsibility toward the planet and one another.
Central to the festival’s programming is Indian Cinema, which continues to serve as the beating heart of IFFI. Highlighting the country’s film-friendly policies and vibrant creative economy, the Indian Panorama section presents a sweeping showcase of 30 feature films, 20 non-feature films and five web series nominated for the Best Web Series (OTT) Award.
The feature line-up encompasses five mainstream films, five works competing for the Best Debut Director of an Indian Feature Film and select titles under the New Horizon segment making their World, International, Asia, or India premieres.
Indian entries also command a strong presence across major competitive categories, including Kantara: A Legend – Chapter 1 (Kannada), Paro – The Untold Story of Bride Slavery (Hindi), and The Kerala Story 2 Goes Beyond (Hindi) in the International Competition, alongside Birds on Ice (Ladakhi) and Sledge (Kashmiri) in the Best Debut Feature Film category, and Kabir Sir ka Akhri Lesson (Hindi), Player 5 (Tamil), and Sev Micchar (Hindi) competing for the ICFT–UNESCO Gandhi Medal.
Furthermore, the festival honours India’s rich cinematic heritage through Centenary Celebrations of classics such as Thulabharam, Sadhi Manase, Waqt, Kashmir Ki Kali, and Chowringhee, Golden Jubilee tributes to Bhakta Kannappa and Kabhi Kabhie, and special homages to veterans Bharathiraja, K. Bhagyaraj, and Nana Patekar, while empowering 100 young practitioners across 13 film crafts through the sixth edition of Creative Minds of Tomorrow (CMOT).
Complementing this celebration of national storytelling is the dedicated Mission Life section, which curates five international films examining ecological shifts, human–non-human relationships, and the urgent need to reimagine sustainable living.
The selection includes María Molina Peiró’s Like Any Other Mortal (Como Todo Mortal), a Netherlands–Spain co-production making its Asia Premiere that blends documentary, flamenco, and science fiction to draw parallels between ancient mining scars in Andalusia and robotic exploration on Mars.
Making its Asia Premiere from Ecuador, Chile, and Germany, Verenice Benítez’s Nunkui follows a young girl in an Amazonian Shuar community who draws strength from ancestral songs, forest spirits, and ecological kinship as mining corporations encroach upon her homeland.
From the Netherlands and Indonesia, Sabine Groenewegen’s The Clearing makes its India Premiere by combining archival and contemporary footage to confront the colonial transformation of Sumatra’s rainforests into rubber plantations and the enduring legacies of exploitation and resistance.
Further enriching the Mission Life slate is Leonardo Pirondi’s Portugal–Brazil experimental sci-fi feature Tropical Fractals (Fractais Tropicais), screening as an India Premiere, which follows space-faring scientists and an artificial intelligence system studying Earth’s final surviving traces as a lone wanderer traverses a ruined planet beginning to heal.
Rounding out the section is renowned Cambodian-French filmmaker Rithy Panh’s We Are the Fruits of the Forest (Nous Sommes les Fruits de la Forêt), an India Premiere documentary that intimately portrays the Indigenous Bunong community in Cambodia’s remote mountains as they strive to safeguard their ancestral traditions and fertile land against corporate encroachment and climate-induced agricultural disruption.
The 57th IFFI weaves together India’s timeless storytelling traditions with urgent global conversations on environmental stewardship, reconfirming cinema’s power to unite cultures across borders.

title: 57th IFFI makes a new beginning with festival’s first-ever ‘Films About Films’ section
subtitle:
Five international productions spanning ten countries to screen in Goa from November 20 to 28

Curated on the suggestion of renowned filmmakers, the debut line-up explores the lives, legacies, and creative journeys behind cinema
content:
Goa, 18 November 2026
Cinema has always been about stories that travel across borders, generations and cultures. But behind every film is another story waiting to be told, that of the filmmaker, the creative process, the struggles and the people who shape it.
Bringing these stories into focus, the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), under this year's theme, “Stories Without Borders”, introduces a new section that turns the spotlight on cinema itself. Through stories of legendary filmmakers, actors and films that were never made, the section offers audiences a chance to explore the many journeys that make cinema what it is.
Stepping behind the camera to explore the stories, storytellers, and creative journeys that bring a motion picture to life, the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) introduces a curated space where cinema becomes both the storyteller and the story. Debuting for the very first time in the festival’s history, the new ‘Films About Films’ segment invites audiences at the 57th IFFI, scheduled to be held in Goa from November 20 to 28 2026, to look closely at the art and craft of filmmaking itself.
Added in response to suggestions from renowned filmmakers with the objective of bringing the art and craft of filmmaking to the forefront, this inaugural segment features five international productions. Spanning productions and co-productions across ten countries, UK, USA, Russia, Georgia, Estonia, Turkey, Switzerland, France, Germany, and Italy, the line-up offers cinephiles a rare look at the lives and legacies that shape world cinema.
The journey begins with a filmmaker whose work has left an enduring mark on the language of cinema.
Directed by Barnaby Thompson,
Maverick: The Epic Adventures of David Lean
(UK, USA | 2026 | English | 105 minutes) explores the life and career of legendary filmmaker David Lean. The documentary looks at his creative vision, ambitious projects and determination to push cinematic boundaries, while also examining the personal struggles behind his professional achievements and his lasting influence on modern cinema.
Moving from the legacy of a celebrated filmmaker to the lives and relationships that shape the stories we tell, the selection turns to a more intimate exploration of human experience.
From Russia,
Raul Geidarov’s Sidney Lumet’s Birthday
(Russia | 2025 | Russian | 92 minutes) follows Dato, a 17-year-old Georgian boy living with his grandmother amid the remains of a once-large family. When his mother unexpectedly returns after a long absence, their quiet routine is disrupted in a story that explores family relationships, growing up and the struggle to remain human through difficult circumstances.
The relationship between life and performance takes centre stage in the next film, where the boundaries between an actor and the character he portrays begin to blur.
Ana Urushadze’s
Supporting Role
(Meorekhariskhovani Roli) (Georgia, Estonia, Turkey, Switzerland, USA | 2026 | Georgian, Armenian | 139 minutes) centres on a celebrated Georgian actor who returns to acting after a long break and auditions for a young director’s first film. Offered an unusual supporting role instead of the heroic characters he is accustomed to playing, he gradually connects with the character in an experience that begins to transform him.
From the personal journey of an actor, the selection moves to a story about a film that never made it to the screen, revealing how cinema is also shaped by the political and historical circumstances surrounding its creation.
In
The Mad Dog of Europe
(France, Germany | 2026 | English | 83 minutes), director Rubika Shah revisits an unproduced screenplay written by Herman J. Mankiewicz in 1932 about a German-Jewish family facing the rise of Hitler and Nazism. Never made by Hollywood studios due to political pressure and commercial interests, the documentary examines the reasons behind its suppression and its relevance in the present context.
Completing this journey through the lives, creative struggles and legacies that shape cinema is a tribute to one of its most influential masters.
Rounding out the lineup,
Francesco Zippel’s Vittorio De Sica - Staging Life
(Italy | 2026 | Italian, French, English, Russian, Farsi | 100 minutes) presents an intimate portrait of Vittorio De Sica, one of the great masters of world cinema. Drawing on rare archival material, family access and testimonies from filmmakers and contemporary artists, the documentary traces his life, work and cinematic legacy.
Together, these five films offer more than a glimpse into the making of cinema. They explore the people behind the camera, the lives that inform performances, the stories that remain untold and the legacies that continue to influence generations of filmmakers. By bringing these diverse journeys together, the new section adds another dimension to IFFI's theme of “Stories Without Borders”, reminding audiences that cinema's reach extends beyond the stories on screen to the creative journeys, historical contexts and human experiences that bring them to life. With its debut, ‘Films About Films’ also creates a space for audiences to engage with the art and craft of filmmaking from a fresh perspective.
The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), scheduled to be held in Goa from 20th to 28th November 2026, will bring together filmmakers, industry professionals and cinema enthusiasts from India and across the world under the theme “Stories Without Borders.”
The newly introduced ‘Films About Films’ section embodies this theme by bringing together stories of filmmakers, actors and cinematic legacies from across countries and cultures, demonstrating how the art of filmmaking itself transcends geographical boundaries.
By exploring the people, ideas and experiences behind cinema, the section highlights the universal creative journeys that connect filmmakers and audiences across the world. With a diverse line-up of Indian and international films, special country showcases, premieres, competitions and industry engagements, IFFI 2026 continues its tradition of celebrating cinematic excellence and promoting cross-cultural exchange through cinema.

title: 57th IFFI 2026 Unveils New Animation Segment to Celebrate the Heart and Soul of Animated Storytelling
subtitle: Five acclaimed international animated features from Japan, France, China, Singapore, and the USA to paint an eclectic canvas of human experience
content:
Goa, 18 November 2026
Across every culture and age, animation has a rare gift for turning simple drawings into stories that move us deeply. Expanding its cinematic horizons, the 57th International Film Festival of India 2026 unveils a dedicated new Animation segment to celebrate the artistry and emotional depth of animated storytelling. Curated with five standout international animated features from Japan, France, China, Singapore, and the USA, the section shines a spotlight on films that move the heart just as much as they dazzle the eye.
Opening a tender window into modern romance and social anxiety is the Japanese animated film
Cherry and Virgin
, directed by Masanao Kawajiri. The 2026 animated feature follows Ryo, a 32-year-old erotic manga artist who struggles to speak to women, and 28-year-old Ami, who finds it equally difficult to interact with men in real life. Despite their fears and lack of romantic experience, the two meet and slowly begin to understand each other, overcoming their insecurities to discover the quiet happiness of a genuine connection.
Blending live-action footage with manga animation, the film is told with disarming warmth and humour. A graduate of Osaka University of Arts, Kawajiri previously earned widespread festival recognition for his 2018 animated short film
A Japanese Boy Who Draws
, establishing a hybrid aesthetic that continues to draw acclaim in Japan and abroad.
Bringing sharp wit and heart to contemporary satire is the French animated film
Jim Queen
, co-directed by Nicolas Athané and Marco Nguyen. Set in Paris, the 2026 animated feature centres on Jim, a popular fitness influencer admired across the city’s gay community, whose world collapses overnight when a mysterious virus named Heterosis begins turning gay men straight, costing him his followers, friends, and social status. With only Lucien, a loyal yet less popular young man, standing by him, Jim sets out through the lively streets of the Marais to find a doctor rumoured to hold a cure. Both directors trained at the renowned Gobelins school of animation. Athané has previously worked on
Rayman
games,
The Rabbi’s Cat
, and
The Red Turtle
alongside co-directing animated series like
Mr Flap
,
Startup Heroes
, and
Peepoodo
, while Nguyen brings rich visual pedigree from his contributions to
The Rabbi’s Cat
,
Ernest & Celestine
, and
The Summit of the Gods
.
Exploring solitude, longing, and attachment in a rapidly changing world is the Chinese animated film
Light Pillar
, the 2026 animated feature debut from writer, director, and production designer Xu Zao. Set in a future where space travel is routine, the film follows Zha, a lonely cleaner tending to the grounds of a bankrupt film studio, who falls in love with a woman inside a lush virtual world. After working extra hours to afford a ticket to join her on the Moon, Zha discovers his ticket is invalid. As a film crew arrives to demolish the old studio for a movie climax, Zha makes the poignant decision to stay behind and fade away alongside the only world he has ever known. Born in Anshan, China, in 1991, Xu Zao holds a master’s degree from the Beijing Film Academy and previously won acclaim for his animated short
No Changes Have Taken in Our Life
, which premiered at IFFR.
From Singapore comes the Chinese-language animated film
Magic Atlas
, a haunting 2026 allegory on memory and resistance directed by Sun Xun. When a mysterious magician arrives in the isolated coal kingdom of Luocha, his presence sparks fear and unrest in an already tense society. Arrested and imprisoned alongside an orphan boy named Xiao Zhi, the magician secretly entrusts the child with a magical atlas just before being burned at the stake during the Mimeng festival, a state ritual in which citizens are made to forget their past. Born in Fuxin, China, in 1980, Sun Xun is a Beijing-based artist and graduate of the China Academy of Fine Arts who founded π Animation Studio in 2005. With works screened at Venice and Berlin,
Magic Atlas
arrives at IFFI following competition runs at the Locarno and Tokyo film festivals.
Rounding out the segment is the English-language American animated film
Ray Gunn
, helmed in 2026 by Academy Award-winning filmmaker Brad Bird. Set in the futuristic metropolis of Metropia, where humans and aliens coexist beneath skies crowded with flying cars and everything comes at a price, widespread corruption lurks behind a gleaming facade. Amid this landscape, Ray Gunn, an old-fashioned private detective struggling to hold onto his values in a world that views his profession as obsolete, finds himself pulled into the biggest case of his career. Celebrated globally as a writer, director, producer, and voice actor who seamlessly weaves emotion, humour, and action, Bird brings the signature storytelling mastery of classics like
The Incredibles
,
Ratatouille
, and
Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol
to this retro-futuristic animated noir.
Through this new segment, the 57th IFFI 2026 invites festival-goers to look beyond the medium and experience animation as an intimate mirror of our hopes, vulnerabilities, and shared humanity.
About IFFI
Established in 1952, the International Film Festival of India is one of Asia’s oldest and prominent international film festivals. Organised by the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, Government of India, in association with the Government of Goa and the Entertainment Society of Goa, IFFI celebrates the best of world cinema while promoting Indian films and talent on a global platform. Held annually in Goa, the festival serves as a platform for creative exchange, discovery of new voices and fostering cultural understanding through cinema.

title: Union Minister of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi inaugurates MSME, KVIC, COIR and NSSH Pavilions at the 45th India International Trade Fair
subtitle:
The theme of the MSME Pavilion this year is “MSME-Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi”

Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises is a vital sector for generation of employment to India's large youth population- Union Minister Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 6:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi, inaugurated the Ministry of MSME, Khadi & Village Industries Commission (KVIC), COIR and National SC-ST Hub (NSSH) Pavilions in Hall No. 6 at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, today. The event was also graced by Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Minister of State in the Ministry of MSME.
The theme of Pavilion this year is “
MSME-Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi”.
Shri Bharat Khera, Secretary, Ministry of MSME and Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner accompanied the delegates. Senior officers from the Ministry of MSME, Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Khadi & Village Industries Commission (KVIC), National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) and COIR Board were also present on the occasion.
Following the inauguration, Union Minister Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi and Minister of State Sushri Shobha Karandlaje visited stalls in the Pavilions and witnessed live demonstration of various traditional manufacturing processes, encouraging the participants and exhibitors.
While speaking to the media, the Union Minister Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi said Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises are vital to provide employment opportunities to India's large youth population. The Government under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has focused on the growth of the MSME sector
. It is one of the highest employment generating sectors. Registration of MSMEs has now crossed 10 crore, generating employment to 42 crore persons. Udyam Assist Portal is making registration easier for micro enterprises.
MSME Pavilion at IITF is a step towards inspiring and encouraging today’s youth to take up entrepreneurship, he added.
Highlights of the Pavilions
MSME Pavilion
The MSME Pavilion features
437 stalls including 292 participating MSME units
from across the country, 101 from KVIC, 34 from NSSH and 10 belonging to Coir sector.
More than 98% of the MSME participants are first-time exhibitors
, providing new entrepreneurs an opportunity to showcase their capabilities.
29 States and Union Territories
are represented, showcasing India's diverse entrepreneurial ecosystem.
57.87% of women entrepreneurs
are participating, highlighting women's growing role in the MSME sector.
27.73% of SC/ST entrepreneurs
are showcasing their products and enterprises.
Entrepreneurs with disabilities (PwD)
are participating, reflecting the spirit of inclusive entrepreneurship.
15 stalls have been set-up by PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries
, providing them with a platform to showcase India's traditional art and craftsmanship.
The MSME Pavilion at IITF 2026 showcases India's rich regional diversity, traditional crafts and evolving manufacturing capabilities through an extensive range of products like-
Textiles, handloom and handicrafts
Green and eco-friendly products
PM Vishwakarma-made products and traditional artisan crafts
Glass, ceramics and metal crafts
Leather goods and beauty products
Games, toys and innovative utility products
Distinctive regional products and other specialized offerings
Bringing together enterprises from
29 States/UTs
, the Pavilion provides a common platform for MSMEs to connect with buyers, visitors and industry stakeholders, fostering product visibility, market access and business opportunities.
The participation of women entrepreneurs, SC/ST entrepreneurs, persons with disabilities and PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries reflects the commitment to inclusive growth and expanding organised marketing opportunities for all enterprises.
The MSME Pavilion not only promotes India's indigenous products and entrepreneurial capabilities but also celebrates the contribution of MSMEs and skilled artisans in strengthening the country's economic and cultural landscape. Technology-focused exhibits showcasing drones and Chandrayaan components developed with MSME participation were displayed by CTTC Bhubaneswar, MSME TC Rohtak, IDEMI Mumbai and IGTR Ahmedabad.
Coir Board Pavilion
The Coir Board Pavilion brings together the two research institutes of the Coir Board, namely the Central Coir Research Institute (CCRI) and the Central Institute of Coir Technology (CICT), along with artisan groups, Coir Board showrooms and sales depots, registered consignors and small-scale manufacturers.
The Pavilion provides a dynamic platform to showcase research outcomes, technological advancements and innovative applications in the coir sector. Key attractions include
soilless cultivation, coir geotextiles, vertical gardens, coir wood, innovative biodegradable products, coir net houses, coir pith composting, CocoLoawn (portable coir-based lawn)
and a
selfie point featuring a coir rope wall
.
National SC-ST Hub (NSSH) Scheme
Under the
National SC-ST Hub (NSSH) Scheme
, 34 SC/ST Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) from seven States have been facilitated with dedicated stalls. The initiative provides participating MSEs with an opportunity to showcase a diverse range of products, including handicrafts, textiles, engineering products and footwear, while connecting with institutional and bulk buyers.
It also supports the achievement of the Central Government's
4% public procurement target from SC/ST-owned MSEs
. Participation in such events offers significant strategic advantages to SC/ST entrepreneurs by enabling them to establish direct business contacts, enhance brand visibility, receive valuable customer feedback and explore new markets, thereby promoting inclusive entrepreneurship and sustainable business growth.
Khadi India Pavilion
The Khadi India Pavilion at IITF 2026 offers an immersive experience of India's rich heritage, traditional craftsmanship and indigenous production processes through
101 stalls
showcasing products made by artisans from different regions of the country. A key attraction this year is a specially created studio for the
“Khadi Ki Baat” podcast
, where conversations will be held with guests, artisans and Khadi enthusiasts to promote awareness and engagement around Khadi.
The Khadi Theme Pavilion also features live demonstrations of traditional charkha, peti charkha, and electrically operated potter's wheel, oil extraction using the traditional kolhu (ghani), handloom weaving and the making of soap, honey products, leather shoes, incense sticks and dhoop.

title: Union Minister Shri Nitin Gadkari highlights role of app-based platforms in employment generation and inclusive mobility
subtitle: Calls upon States to adopt Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines, 2025 to strengthen driver welfare and passenger services
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 11:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways, Shri Nitin Gadkari, today addressed the gathering at
‘RIDE – MOVING INDIA FORWARD’
at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Organised in collaboration with Uber, Ola, Rapido, Bharat Taxi, Zomato, Swiggy and Porter, the programme brought together industry representatives, drivers, gig workers and beneficiaries to highlight the contribution of app-based platforms to employment generation, mobility services and livelihood opportunities. The programme was attended by Shri Pavan Guntupalli, Co-Founder, Rapido; Shri Shiva Shailendran, Director, Uber India; Shri Uttam Diga, CEO, Porter; Shri Ankush Aggarwal, Business Head, Ola; Ms. Neha Singhvi, Vice President, Swiggy; Shri Jaskiran Bedi, Public Policy, Zomato; and actor and speaker Shri Sharad Kelkar.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Nitin Gadkari emphasised the role of technology, innovation, entrepreneurship and digital platforms in creating employment opportunities and addressing socio-economic challenges. He noted that app-based services have expanded beyond passenger transportation to include goods delivery and food services, creating new avenues of livelihood for people from diverse backgrounds.
The Minister highlighted the importance of wider adoption of the Motor Vehicle Aggregator framework by States to facilitate employment opportunities, particularly for people from socially, economically and educationally disadvantaged sections. He called upon State Governments to provide an enabling environment for such services and encourage greater participation in the emerging mobility ecosystem.
Emphasising the importance of technology in improving livelihoods, Shri Gadkari cited the introduction of mechanism-driven e-rickshaws and e-carts as examples of technological interventions that have transformed traditional occupations and reduced physical hardship. He also stressed the need to strengthen last-mile connectivity, particularly in rural areas, enabling people to access education, employment and markets more easily and transport agricultural produce to urban centres.
The Minister observed that the objective of the Government's policy framework was to facilitate the growth of the sector while safeguarding the interests of drivers and consumers. He encouraged industry stakeholders to work closely with the Government and share suggestions for further improving the regulatory framework. He underlined that the benefits of technological progress should reach all sections of society and contribute to the broader vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
Earlier, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Shri C. N. Singh, outlined key provisions of the Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines, 2025, revised following consultations with State Governments, aggregators and other stakeholders.
The guidelines introduce several measures to strengthen driver welfare and improve service standards. These include a minimum 80 per cent share of the applicable fare for drivers using their own vehicles, health insurance coverage of ₹5 lakh and term insurance of at least ₹10 lakh. Other provisions include permitting drivers to work across multiple aggregator platforms, 40 hours of induction training and appointment of a 24x7 grievance officer through the aggregator's call centre to address complaints from drivers and passengers.
Shri Singh highlighted that the guidelines seek to strengthen driver welfare, improve service standards and establish accessible grievance redressal mechanisms. He observed that drivers are important participants in the digital mobility ecosystem and that their welfare, dignity and working conditions are essential to the sustainable development of the sector.
The programme also featured experiences of individuals from diverse backgrounds who have benefited from app-based platforms. Women beneficiaries shared their journeys towards financial independence, while drivers and other platform workers highlighted the opportunities these platforms have created for employment, entrepreneurship, business expansion and improved last-mile connectivity.
A presentation on road safety and the Government's
Rah-Veer Scheme
was also made to sensitise participants about the importance of providing timely assistance to road accident victims. On the occasion, Shri Nitin Gadkari felicitated gig workers and drivers who had helped save lives by taking injured road accident victims to hospitals during the critical hours following road accidents.
Drivers, representatives of participating platforms, industry leaders and women beneficiaries who have achieved notable success through these platforms were also felicitated during the programme.

title: Ministry of Rural Development Issues Ombudsperson Guidelines to Strengthen Transparency and Accountability under VB-G RAM G
subtitle:
Stronger Grievance Redressal Mechanism to Safeguard Rural Workers’ Rights under VB-G RAM G

Digital Monitoring, Social Audits and Citizen Participation to Strengthen Accountability under VB-G RAM G
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 10:29AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Rural Development has strengthened the framework for transparency, accountability and citizen participation in the implementation of the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, through the Guidelines for Ombudsperson and Appellate Authority.
The guidelines reinforce the spirit of the VB- G RAM G Act by strengthening institutional mechanisms to safeguard workers’ statutory rights, address implementation-related grievances and promote accountable delivery of programme benefits. The Ombudsperson will serve as an important link in the programme’s accountability framework, providing rural citizens with an accessible mechanism to raise complaints and seek appropriate redressal.
A dedicated Ombudsperson at the district level will address grievances relating to job cards, employment, wage payments, delay compensation, worksite facilities, muster rolls and denial of statutory entitlements. The guidelines also cover discrimination, harassment and violations of workers’ rights, including those of women and vulnerable groups, ensuring that such concerns receive due attention.
The guidelines strengthen the institutional capacity of Ombudspersons through an expanded pool of eligible candidates with experience in rural development, public administration, law, academics, social work and management. Provisions relating to tenure and remuneration have also been revised to support continuity and effective functioning. Emphasis has been placed on field visits, community engagement and familiarity with digital platforms.
A key feature is the dedicated digital platform for Ombudspersons, which will facilitate online registration and tracking of complaints, recording of proceedings, uploading of awards and monitoring of action taken. Geo-tagged and time-stamped photographs during field visits will further strengthen documentation, traceability and transparency in the grievance redressal process.
The guidelines also reinforce the role of social audit as a vital mechanism for community-led transparency and accountability. Ombudspersons will attend at least three Social Audit public hearings or Gram Sabhas every month, providing an opportunity to hear citizens’ concerns directly and facilitate appropriate follow-up. Social audit findings and community feedback, along with individual grievances, will support the identification of discrepancies and corrective action in accordance with prescribed procedures.
The Ombudsperson and Appellate Authority framework complements other accountability measures under VB–G RAM G, including digital monitoring, public disclosure and social audit. Together, these mechanisms aim to promote transparent implementation, strengthen oversight and ensure that grievances are addressed through a structured and accountable process.
Through these guidelines, the Government seeks to further strengthen citizen-centric governance under VB–G RAM G, ensuring that rural workers have accessible avenues for grievance redressal and that implementation remains transparent, responsive and accountable.

title: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Launches Curtain Raiser for India International Science Festival (IISF) 2026, Calls for Taking Science Beyond Labs to Empower Youth and Startups
subtitle:
Pune to Host the 12th Edition of IISF Across Five Premier Research and Academic Campuses from December 19–22 Under the Theme "India’s Science, World’s Future"

Under PM Modi’s Vision of Vishwa Bandhu Bharat, Indian Science Is Delivering Solutions for All Humanity, From Indigenous Bio-Experiments on the ISS to Frontier Biotech: Dr. Jitendra Singh

India Has Reimagined Its National Science Calendar Around Two Distinct Flagship Pillars, Academic Conclave ESTIC in New Delhi and Public-Centric Festival IISF Across the Country, Says Union Minister

Nationwide Build-Up Across 13 Cities with Vijnana Bharati (VIBHA) Will Connect Students, Women, Farmers, and Entrepreneurs with Working Laboratories Ahead of Pune Mega Event: Dr. Jitendra Singh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 6:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today formally launched the Curtain Raiser for the 12th edition of the India International Science Festival (IISF) 2026, alongside unveiling the official festival website and brochure, at the National Media Centre in New Delhi.
Addressing the gathering, Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that IISF 2026, scheduled to be held in Pune from December 19 to 22 under the theme "India’s Science, World’s Future" (Bharat ka Vigyan, Vishwa ka Bhavishya), embodies Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Vishwa Bandhu Bharat, where Indian scientific breakthroughs serve the welfare of the entire humankind. Explaining that the theme is already being translated into action rather than remaining a slogan, the Minister cited indigenous research kits developed by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT) and carried to the International Space Station (ISS) by Indian astronaut Shubhanshu Shukla, whose experimental outcomes will benefit the whole world. As India moves toward a frontline global position on the path to Viksit Bharat 2047, Dr. Jitendra Singh added, Indian science will increasingly shape the global scientific ecosystem.
The curtain raiser ceremony, organised by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Ministry of Science & Technology, in collaboration with Vijnana Bharati (VIBHA), was graced on the dais by Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood; Secretary, Department of Biotechnology, Dr. Rajesh S. Gokhale; and National Organising Secretary, Vijnana Bharati (VIBHA), Dr. Shiv Kumar Sharma.
Secretary, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) and Director General, CSIR, Dr. N. Kalaiselvi; Secretary, Department of Science and Technology (DST), Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare; Secretary, and Director, BRIC–National Centre for Cell Science (NCCS), Pune, Dr. Thomas Pucadyil, along with senior scientists, institutional directors, and officials from participating departments, also attended the event.
Speaking on the strategic transformation of India’s scientific engagements over the past few years, Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that the government took a conscious decision to replace scattered, repetitive gatherings, including the erstwhile Indian Science Congress, with two flagship national events carrying distinct identities. While the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC), inaugurated annually by the Prime Minister in New Delhi with the participation of over 13 ministries and Nobel Laureates, serves as an academic-driven conclave exploring frontier themes, IISF brings a festive, public-facing character with international resonance. By rotating the venue to different regions, after Chandigarh, Hyderabad, Goa, and Delhi, bringing IISF for the first time to Pune leverages the western hub’s vibrant academic, research, and industrial ecosystem.
Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that IISF 2026 is designed to communicate complex, futuristic domains, ranging from gene editing, antibodies, and insulin production to next-generation energy sources and an immersive, larger-than-life walk-through 3D cell, in an engaging format tailored for diverse stakeholders. Beyond academic talks, including a special lecture by 2001 Nobel Laureate Sir Tim Hunt, the festival creates dedicated pathways for children, youth, women, existing and aspiring startups, entrepreneurs, and industry through B2B meetings, hackathons, and science safaris so young minds can discover their aptitudes and turn ideas into enterprises.
Commending Vijnana Bharati (VIBHA) and Dr. Shiv Kumar Sharma for championing a "whole-of-government, whole-of-science, whole-of-nation, and whole-of-society" approach, Dr. Jitendra Singh lauded VIBHA’s pivotal role in spearheading curtain raiser events across 13 cities, including Chennai, Kolkata, Dehradun, Thiruvananthapuram, Pune, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Imphal, Indore, Mohali, and Ahmedabad, leading up to the Pune festival. He also urged media representatives to actively participate in and travel to Pune to carry India’s science story to every corner of the country.
Principal Scientific Adviser Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood described IISF 2026 as a unique celebration of science as a collective national endeavour aimed at bringing young people into the scientific fold and embedding scientific temper into public consciousness beyond research laboratories. Connecting the tagline Bharat ka Vigyan, Vishwa ka Bhavishya with India’s timeless philosophy of VasudhaivaKutumbakam, Prof. Sood stated that India has repeatedly demonstrated its willingness to share homegrown innovations at scale, from Vaccine Maitri to Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), and expressed confidence that the energy of IISF 2026 will inspire youth to drive cutting-edge, people-centric innovations for Viksit Bharat.
In his welcome remarks, DBT Secretary Dr. Rajesh S. Gokhale stated that since its inception in 2015, IISF has belonged to the people, uniting curious students, inspiring teachers, small-town innovators, and farmers practising everyday soil engineering. Describing IISF at its core as a platform connecting Samaj, Sarkar, aur Bazaar (Society, Government, and Market) through science, where societal needs guide research, government empowers innovation, and markets convert discoveries into public goods, Dr. Gokhale informed that the 2026 edition brings together major science departments alongside the Department of Atomic Energy and NITI Aayog’s Atal Innovation Mission (AIM).
During the programme, BRIC–NCCS Director Dr. Thomas Pucadyil presented the detailed blueprint of IISF 2026, which will be held under the banner "One Nation, One Science Festival" across five closely located campuses in Pune: BRIC–National Centre for Cell Science (NCCS), CSIR–National Chemical Laboratory (NCL), Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER) Pune, Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), and COEP Technological University.

title: MSDE Engages with UN Special Rapporteur on advancing inclusive skilling and economic participation of persons with disabilities
subtitle: Dialogue focuses on accessible training, meaningful employment and pathways to economic independence
ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) held an interaction with Ms. Heba Hagrass, United Nations Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, on strengthening disability inclusion in skill development and expanding pathways to employment and entrepreneurship. The engagement formed part of the Special Rapporteur’s official visit to India.
The interaction provided an opportunity to examine how skill development systems can support the dignity, autonomy and economic participation of persons with disabilities. The dialogue centred on addressing barriers across the journey from access to training and certification to employment, retention and career progression, in keeping with the principles of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD).
Speaking on the engagement, Shri Niranjan Kumar Sudhansu, Additional Secretary, MSDE said,
“An inclusive skill ecosystem must recognise both the diversity of learners and the equal worth of their aspirations. For persons with disabilities, access to training must translate into the freedom to choose a vocation, demonstrate competence and progress in the world of work. Our endeavour is to embed accessibility across the skilling journey and strengthen the connection between learning and livelihoods. The measure of our progress must be the opportunities people are able to exercise and the economic independence they are able to achieve.”
The engagement brought into focus the importance of accessible training infrastructure, digital learning platforms, learning materials and assessment processes. Reasonable accommodation, assistive technologies and the capacity of trainers and assessors were identified as important considerations in enabling learners with different disabilities to participate on an equal basis. The discussions also underscored the importance of embedding accessibility and appropriate support within mainstream training programmes, alongside disability-specific interventions, to enable greater participation and inclusion.
The dialogue also addressed the relationship between skilling and labour market inclusion. Industry engagement, accessible workplaces and support during the transition from training to employment are critical to ensuring that acquired skills lead to sustained livelihoods. The discussions also emphasised upon the enabling measures to enhance the participation of persons with disabilities in skill training and government employment, while encouraging greater inclusion and employment opportunities in the private sector.
Entrepreneurship and self-employment were also discussed as important pathways to economic independence, including the role of access to finance, mentoring, technology and markets in supporting entrepreneurs with disabilities.
Ms. Heba Hagrass, United Nations Special Rapporteur on the rights of persons with disabilities said
,
“The right to work begins with having a real opportunity to learn, choose and participate. Inclusive vocational training must equip persons with disabilities for the full range of opportunities in a changing economy, with accessibility and reasonable accommodation built into its design. Meaningful participation of persons with disabilities and their representative organisations is essential to this process. Their experience and expertise can help institutions translate commitments into practical changes that advance equality and independence.”
The dialogue also highlighted the role of evidence in strengthening disability inclusion, including through better understanding of participation, training outcomes and pathways to employment. Particular attention was drawn to addressing barriers faced by women with disabilities and persons in rural and underserved areas.
The engagement situated inclusive skilling within the wider objective of enabling persons with disabilities to participate as equal contributors to economic and social development. It provided a platform for exchanging perspectives on how policy, institutional practice, technology and employer participation can work together to expand opportunity.
The United Nations Special Rapporteur on the rights of persons with disabilities is an independent expert appointed by the Human Rights Council. The mandate promotes the rights of persons with disabilities through dialogue, country visits, recommendations and the exchange of good practices.

title: National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction Strengthens India’s Efforts Towards a Drug-Free Society
subtitle:
Focuses on Preventive Education, Awareness, Identification, Counselling, Treatment, Rehabilitation and Social Reintegration

Article 47 of the Constitution Mandates the State to Endeavour to Prohibit Consumption of Intoxicating Drinks and Drugs Injurious to Health
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has been implementing a scheme for the prevention of alcoholism and substance abuse since 1985-86, reflecting its sustained commitment towards addressing substance dependence through preventive, therapeutic and rehabilitative interventions. This is in accordance with its Constitutional mandate and commitment to address alcoholism and substance abuse while building a healthy, inclusive and socially empowered society.
The Article 47 of the Constitution directs the State to endeavour to bring about prohibition of the consumption, except for medicinal purposes, of intoxicating drinks and drugs that are injurious to health.
A Senior Official in the Ministry said the magnitude of the challenge was highlighted by the first National Survey on the Extent and Pattern of Substance Use in India, conducted in 2018 by the National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC), AIIMS, New Delhi, and released in February 2019. The survey provided important insights into the extent and pattern of substance use across the country and underscored the need for comprehensive interventions, he said.
According to the survey, approximately 16 crore people consumed alcohol in India, of whom more than 5.7 crore required assistance for harmful or dependent use. Around 3.1 crore people used cannabis products, while 2.26 crore used opioids. Of these, approximately 25 lakh individuals were dependent on cannabis, while nearly 77 lakh required assistance for opioid use, the Official informed.
The Official added the survey further revealed that more than 7 crore individuals were affected by substance use disorders, including nearly 1.2 crore children and 58 lakh women, highlighting the importance of sustained awareness, early intervention, accessible treatment and rehabilitation services.
The Official said the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) has been designed to address the multifaceted challenges associated with substance use through a comprehensive and coordinated approach.
The Ministry continues to strengthen preventive and rehabilitative efforts while promoting a compassionate, supportive and inclusive approach towards individuals affected by substance use disorders, he added.
He said that NAPDDR is implemented as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with Central Sector components and focuses on two key objectives.
The Official said the first objective is to reduce drug demand through preventive education, awareness generation, identification, counselling, treatment and rehabilitation. The second objective is to reduce the stigma and discrimination associated with drug dependence, which often create barriers to the social acceptance and reintegration of affected individuals, he said.
He said the Plan recognises that addressing substance dependence requires not only treatment and rehabilitation but also an enabling social environment in which individuals can seek assistance without fear of discrimination or exclusion.
The Official said the awareness generation and preventive education play a significant role in informing individuals, families and communities about the harmful consequences of substance use. Early identification and timely counselling, along with access to appropriate treatment and rehabilitation facilities, are essential components of the national response, the Official said.
He further said that reducing stigma and discrimination is equally important to ensure that individuals recovering from substance dependence can return to their families and communities and participate meaningfully in society.
The Official said with its focus on prevention, awareness, treatment, rehabilitation and social reintegration, the Ministry is working towards building a healthier and drug-free society, in alignment with the constitutional vision and the broader goal of inclusive socio-economic development.

title: One-day capacity building workshop on “Strengthening Sub-National SDG Monitoring” organised in Kolkata, West Bengal
subtitle:
MoSPI is accelerating India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047 through robust Sustainable Development Goal monitoring framework at the State and UT levels

The workshop focuses on strengthening State/UT Indicator Frameworks by supporting States/UTs currently developing their indicator frameworks and featuring sub-national monitoring best practices
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), in collaboration with the Department of Planning, Statistics and Programme Monitoring, Government of West Bengal and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), organised a one-day Capacity Building Workshop on “Strengthening Sub-National SDG Monitoring” in Kolkata, West Bengal on 18th November, 2026. The workshop brought together government officials from States and Union Territories that are in process of development of their respective State/UT Indicator Frameworks (SIFs/UTIFs) and the three (3) States/UT sharing best practices, with the aim of strengthening institutional capacities and providing targeted technical support to advance the process. Around 50 participants attended the workshop, comprising officers from MoSPI, UNDP, and States/UTs-West Bengal, Maharashtra, Delhi, Odisha, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
With around four years remaining to achieve the 2030 Agenda, strengthening sub-national monitoring systems is critical to advancing SDG localisation and translating national commitments into measurable outcomes at the State/UT levels. State/UT-level monitoring enables governments to track progress against SDG targets, identify development gaps and align policies and interventions with local priorities.
As per SDGs-National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2026, 33 States and Union Territories have developed their respective State/UT Indicator Frameworks. Strengthening the remaining frameworks and improving existing monitoring systems is important to ensure comprehensive SDG monitoring across the country.
In the inaugural session, Ms. Supriya Roy, Additional Director General, Social Statistics Division, MoSPI, emphasised the importance of strengthening monitoring systems at the State and local levels. She highlighted that national-level data alone cannot capture the diversity of development challenges across India. State and District Indicator Frameworks are essential to translate national SDG commitments into locally relevant priorities and measurable outcomes. She also underlined the need to strengthen statistical capacities and improve the quality and timeliness of data.
Shri Pawan Kadyan, Senior Special Secretary, Department of Finance, Government of West Bengal, highlighted the need for State Indicator Frameworks to reflect ground realities and local development priorities. He emphasised that monitoring should extend to districts, blocks and Gram Sabhas. He also stressed the need to move beyond tracking scheme implementation and fund utilisation towards measuring actual development outcomes, enabling a shift towards outcome-oriented governance. Representative of UNDP, Mr. Jaimon Uthup, Policy Specialist emphasized the commitment to supporting the Government of India and States/UTs in building robust data systems, technical capacities, and inclusive monitoring mechanisms.
Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), MoSPI, highlighted the ongoing statistical reforms undertaken by MoSPI to address emerging data needs and strengthen the evidence base for development planning. He emphasised the importance of linking Indicator Frameworks not only with the SDGs but also with India's longer-term development goals under Viksit Bharat. He noted that updated base years and new statistical surveys to capture the unorganised sector and services economy are strengthening the country's statistical system.
The technical sessions commenced with a presentation by Ms. Ruchika Gupta, Deputy Director General, Social Statistics Division, MoSPI, on strengthening the SDG monitoring architecture at national and sub-national levels. The session covered the National Indicator Framework (NIF), its alignment with State/UT Indicator Frameworks, principles for indicator selection, data sources, reporting periodicity and institutional responsibilities.
A key component of the workshop was the sharing of good practices and experiences from States that have made progress in strengthening SDG monitoring and localisation. Representatives from Maharashtra, Delhi and Odisha presented their approaches, highlighting institutional arrangements, data systems and lessons that could inform the development and strengthening of State/UT Indicator Frameworks.
Officials from the participating State and UT administrations presented their progress, institutional preparedness, data readiness and challenges in developing their respective frameworks. The discussions helped identify State/UT-specific priorities, institutional requirements and data-related gaps.
The workshop also included a facilitated group exercise led by MoSPI and UNDP, focusing on the development and refinement of draft State/UT Indicator Frameworks. Participants reviewed potential indicators for each SDG, identified State/UT-specific indicators reflecting local development priorities, mapped responsible departments and data sources, and assessed data availability and gaps. The exercise also emphasised the integration of gender-responsive and disaggregated indicators, wherever relevant, and the prioritisation of indicators based on relevance and monitoring requirements.
The workshop concluded with discussions on key recommendations and next steps for finalising and strengthening the respective State/UT Indicator Frameworks. MoSPI and UNDP reaffirmed their commitment to providing continued technical support to the all States/UTs.
The workshop reiterated the importance of robust sub-national statistical systems in advancing SDG localisation and evidence-based policymaking. State and UT Indicator Frameworks provide a common basis for tracking progress against the SDGs while reflecting local development priorities and longer-term Vision 2047 agendas. These frameworks can also strengthen planning, monitoring and decision-making at State and sub-State levels

A robust league structure is envisaged to provide regular, high-quality competitive pathways for talent identification and athlete development, while simultaneously driving private investment and generating employment across sports management, broadcasting, technology, events, and allied services.
While several sports leagues in the country have achieved varying levels of success, many disciplines with strong sporting and social potential face commercial viability hurdles during their initial stages. Accordingly, the Committee will assess the present sports league ecosystem to identify the major issues and constraints affecting the establishment and sustainability of leagues, and will identify priority sports and categories, particularly Olympic sports, women's sports, youth sports, indigenous sports, and emerging sports, to recommend suitable operational models tailored to their sporting and commercial potential. To bridge this gap, the Committee will examine mechanisms for structured Government facilitation alongside active participation from the private sector, sports organisations, State Governments, local bodies, and communities. This includes evaluating targeted interventions such as Viability Gap Funding (VGF), direct and indirect financial assistance, and concessional access to Government sports infrastructure.
The Committee has been mandated to assess existing ecosystem constraints, identify priority sports and tailored operational models, and recommend measures to attract corporate capital, franchise ownership, sponsorships, broadcasting and digital rights, and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) financing. Additionally, the committee will propose strategies to integrate leagues with schools, colleges, universities, and local clubs to foster grassroots participation among youth and women, alongside establishing an institutional governance framework covering financial transparency, athlete welfare, integrity, and a phased implementation roadmap informed by global best practices.
