title: From ASEAN to Europe: India's Exports Gain Momentum Across FTA Partners and Beyond
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 3:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India's exports to key FTA partners and major trading markets recorded broad-based growth during April–September FY 2026–27. Exports to ASEAN surged 58% to US$ 28.06 billion, while shipments to SAFTA partners rose 22% to US$ 15.29 billion. Exports to the European Union increased 5% to US$ 38.79 billion. Strong growth in Singapore, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, Japan, South Korea and Oman, alongside gains in other European markets, reflected India's widening export footprint and strengthening trade linkages across global markets.
Introduction
India's exports to key
Free Trade Agreement (FTA)
partners and major trade-partner markets recorded broad-based growth during April-September FY 2026-27. Strong export performance across
ASEAN, South Asia, East Asia
and several
European markets
reflected the growing geographical diversification of India's trade.
Among the major export destinations,
Singapore, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, Oman, Italy and Spain
registered particularly strong growth. ASEAN emerged as a significant contributor to the overall expansion, while neighbouring South Asian markets recorded sustained growth.
Exports to developed markets, including the
European Union, Japan, South Korea, Australia and the United Kingdom,
also increased during the period. The performance across these markets highlights the widening geographical spread of India's exports and its expanding trade linkages.
ASEAN Emerges as a Major Growth Engine
India's exports to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) recorded significant growth during the first half of FY 2026-27. Under the CECA framework,
exports to ASEAN increased 58%
,
from US$ 17.75 billion
in April-September FY 2025-26
to
US$ 28.06 billion
in the corresponding period of FY 2026-27.
Singapore
emerged as one of the strongest-performing markets in the region. India's exports to Singapore more than doubled, increasing
103%
from US$ 5.45 billion to
US$ 11.07 billion.
Malaysia
also registered a substantial increase, with
exports rising 83%
from US$ 3.05 billion to US$ 5.58 billion
during the period
Exports to Vietnam increased 36% to US$ 3.83 billion
, while shipments to
Indonesia
rose
36%
to
US$ 2.98 billion
.
Thailand
remained another important export destination, with shipments valued at
US$ 2.65 billion.
Exports to SAFTA Partners Rise 22%
Exports to South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA)
partners also recorded growth during April-September FY 2026-27.
Total exports to SAFTA markets increased 22%,
from US$ 12.55 billion to US$ 15.29 billion
during the corresponding period.
Sri Lanka
emerged as a major growth market, with
exports rising 73% from US$ 2.28 billion to US$ 3.94 billion.
Exports to
Nepal
increased
19%, from US$ 3.66 billion to
US$ 4.37 billion
.
Bhutan
also recorded growth of
16%,
with exports reaching
US$ 711.4 million.
Among smaller South Asian markets,
Maldives
registered strong growth of
52%
, with exports increasing
from US$ 222.2 million to
US$ 337.4 million.
Bangladesh
remained
India's largest export destination within SAFTA
, with shipments valued at
US$ 5.66 billion
, registering growth of
2%.
Japan and South Korea Strengthen East Asian Export Momentum
India's exports
to Japan and South Korea
recorded notable increases during April-September FY 2026-27, contributing to the broader expansion of trade across Asian markets.
Exports to Japan increased 40%,
from US$ 2.92 billion to
US$ 4.10 billion
during the period.
Similarly,
exports to South Korea increased 24%,
from US$ 3.15 billion to
US$ 3.91 billion.
The strong growth in both markets adds to the broader momentum across India's Asian trade partners, alongside the sizable increases recorded in
Singapore, Malaysia, Vietnam
and
Indonesia
.
EFTA Markets Maintain Positive Export Growth
India's exports to
European Free Trade Association (EFTA) partners
increased by approximately
5%,
from US$ 980.2 million to
US$ 1.03 billion
during April-September FY 2026-27.
Switzerland remained India's largest export destination among EFTA partners.
Exports to the country increased
11%
, reaching
US$ 758.4 million.
Norway
also recorded positive growth, with exports increasing
14% to US$ 264.0 million.
Liechtenstein
registered
30%
export growth, although from a relatively smaller base.
European Union Markets Record Steady Growth
Total exports to the European Union (EU) increased 5%,
from US$ 36.97 billion to
US$ 38.79 billion,
supported by growth across several major European destinations.
Spain
emerged as one of the strongest-performing markets, with exports increasing
45%
from US$ 3.23 billion to
US$ 4.68 billion
.
Italy
also recorded substantial growth, with Indian exports rising
25%
, from US$ 3.63 billion to
US$ 4.55 billion.
Germany
remained a major European export destination, recording growth of
12%
, with exports reaching
US$ 6.34 billion
.
Exports to
France
increased
9%
to
US$ 3.73 billion
.
Several smaller European markets, including
Croatia, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Estonia
and the
Czech Republic
, also registered particularly strong growth during the period.
New-Generation Trade Partners Add to Export Momentum
Beyond ASEAN, South Asia and major East Asian and European markets, India's exports to several other trading partners also recorded positive growth during April-September FY 2026-27.
Oman
registered particularly strong growth, with exports increasing
47%
, from US$ 2.23 billion to
US$ 3.29 billion
.
Exports to
Australia
increased
11%
, from US$ 3.69 billion to
US$ 4.10 billion.
The
United Kingdom
also recorded positive growth, with Indian exports rising
7%
, from US$ 6.83 billion to
US$ 7.32 billion
.
Mauritius
witnessed a notable increase of
45%
, with exports reaching
US$ 346.2 million
during the period.
New-Generation Trade Partners Add to Export Momentum
India's export performance during April-September FY 2026-27 reflects sustained growth across several FTA partner markets and major trading destinations.
ASEAN emerged as a particularly dynamic region, driven by the doubling of exports to Singapore and substantial increases in shipments to
Malaysia, Vietnam and Indonesia
.
South Asian markets also contributed to the expansion, with
Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan and Maldives registering positive growth
. At the same time, increased exports to
Japan, South Korea, Oman, Australia
and
several European markets
demonstrated the widening geographical spread of India's export destinations.
The broad-based growth across traditional and emerging markets highlights the increasing diversification of
India's export footprint and strengthening trade linkages across Asia, Europe and other major global markets.

title: India's Wind Energy Transition
subtitle: Charting Path towards 156 GW  and Beyond
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 NOV 2026 11:00AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Wind Energy: Expanding Capacity, Strengthening Energy Security
Wind energy is emerging as a key pillar of India’s transition towards a cleaner and more sustainable energy future.
By harnessing the natural movement of air to generate electricity, wind power offers a renewable alternative to fossil fuels
. It can help meet growing electricity demand while reducing dependence on conventional energy sources. As India expands its renewable energy capacity, wind energy is becoming increasingly important for building a diverse, resilient and low-carbon
emission
system.
As of 30 September 2026, India’s total installed renewable energy capacity stood at
299.25 GW
. Wind power accounted for
59.20 GW
, representing approximately
19.8% of the total
installed renewable energy capacity. Between March 2014 and September 2026, installed wind capacity grew from 21 GW to 59.20 GW,
nearly a 2.8-fold increase
, reflecting wind energy’s growing role in India’s renewable electricity mix.
With continued capacity addition, technological advancement and supportive government initiatives, wind energy is expected to remain a key pillar of India’s efforts to diversify its energy mix, strengthen energy security and achieve its renewable energy targets.
India’s Wind Energy Landscape
India’s wind energy sector is expanding steadily with rising installed capacity and strong wind resource potential across key states. It is increasingly supported by domestic manufacturing and its role in meeting renewable energy targets.
Wind Resource Potential
India's estimated
gross wind power potential is 695.5 GW at 120 metres
and
1,163.9 GW at 150 metres
above ground level.
Majority of the assessed wind potential at 150 Meter is concentrated in eight high-resource states:
Rajasthan:
284.2 GW;
Gujarat:
180.8 GW;
Maharashtra
: 173.9 GW;
Karnataka:
169.3 GW;
Andhra Pradesh
: 123.3 GW;
Tamil Nadu:
95.1 GW;
Madhya Pradesh:
55.4 GW;
Telangana:
54.7 GW.
More than 900
wind-monitoring stations
have been installed nationwide by NIWE to map wind resources and identify high-potential sites for wind energy development.
Wind potential maps have been developed at
50 m, 80 m, 100 m, 120 m, and 150 m hub heights
.
India's vast wind resource base provides a strong foundation for achieving
100 GW wind capacity by 2030
and
156 GW by 2036.
Wind Capacity and Manufacturing Growth
India ranks
4th globally
in installed wind power capacity.
Wind energy capacity has more than doubled over the past 12 years.
An additional
28 GW
is under implementation.
India recorded its
highest-ever annual wind capacity addition of 6.05 GW in 2025-26
, surpassing the previous record of
5.4 GW in 2016-17
.
Nearly
45% of wind generation occurs during peak demand hours
, complementing solar power and strengthening grid reliability.
Wind Turbine Manufacturing Capacity
has increased from 10 GW in 2014 to about 24 GW, as on March 2026.
The sector has achieved
70-80% indigenisation
across key components.
Strong domestic supply chains exist for blades, towers, gearboxes, and other critical equipment.
India generated 106.7 billion units of wind power in FY 2025–26, reflecting its contribution to the country's electricity supply.
Wind energy is becoming a more stable and integrated part of India’s power system.
Its role will expand further with technological upgrades and diversified deployment.
Key Government Interventions
Government priorities focus on expanding wind deployment, offshore development, and grid modernisation. These are supported by targeted schemes, financial incentives, and regulatory reforms.
₹
6,853 crore
Viability Gap Funding (VGF)
approved for
1,000 MW of offshore wind projects
, comprising
500 MW each off the coasts of Gujarat and Tamil Nadu
.
Generation Based Incentive (GBI) Scheme
was available for projects commissioned before March, 2017.
A
500 MW pilot project
launched under the
Contracts for Difference (CfD)
. CfD is a mechanism designed to reduce price volatility and provide revenue certainty to renewable energy developers.
A
Task Force constituted
in
January 2026
to address regulatory, land, transmission, and implementation challenges.
Dedicated wind component introduced under
Renewable Purchase Obligations (RPOs)
to ensure sustained demand.
Green Energy Open Access Rules
introduced to facilitate direct procurement of renewable power by industries.
Implementation of the
Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM)
, transparent bidding guidelines, and Late Payment Surcharge Rules has strengthened investor confidence.
Promotion of hybrid and
Round-the-Clock (RTC) Renewable Energy
projects to improve grid efficiency.
Priorities for Wind Energy include:
Expanding wind deployment into emerging states such as Madhya Pradesh, Telangana, and Odisha.
Launching India's offshore wind sector through identified leasing areas in Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.
Integrating wind power into
Round-the-Clock (RTC) Renewable Energy
solutions through storage-linked business models.
Modernising the grid and deploying
Artificial Intelligence (AI)
-based forecasting tools for renewable energy management.
Strengthening domestic manufacturing across the entire wind energy value chain.
Global Partnerships in Wind Energy
India is strengthening wind energy cooperation with the UK, Denmark, Belgium, Germany and EU to accelerate sector development. These partnerships focus on offshore wind deployment, advanced technology transfer, and improved grid integration. They also enable knowledge sharing on policy design, financing models, and project execution.
India–United Kingdom:
The
India–United Kingdom Offshore Wind Taskforce
was launched in February 2026 under
Vision 2035
and the
Fourth India–UK Energy Dialogue
.
Focus areas include market design, port infrastructure, supply chains, and blended finance.
India-Belgium:
At the World Economic Forum (WEF) 2026, India and Belgium reaffirmed cooperation in offshore wind, research and development, and green taxonomy, signalling growing European interest in India's clean energy transition.
India-Denmark:
India signed a cooperation agreement with Denmark's
Ministry for Energy, Utilities and Climate
in 2019 for offshore wind capacity building.
The bilateral
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)
was renewed in May 2025.
Cooperation now includes power system modelling, integration of variable renewable energy, and joint expert training.
The Road Ahead for Wind Energy
As India enters the next phase of its energy transition, wind power will play an increasingly important role in delivering reliable, affordable, and domestically sourced clean electricity. The country's extensive onshore and offshore wind resources provide a strong foundation for long-term growth, but realizing this opportunity will require faster project execution, stronger transmission infrastructure, improved forecasting capabilities, and continued policy support. By expanding into new geographies, integrating wind with storage and round-the-clock power solutions, and strengthening domestic manufacturing and export competitiveness, India can position wind energy not only as a key contributor to its climate and energy security goals, but also as a driver of industrial development and economic growth.
